articles.title: The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure
articles.summary:
The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure
We moved a copy of 99.99999% of GitHub’s repositories to Azure. Here’s how per-reference quorums will bring over the rest, and how object storage lets reads scale independently.
Over the past year, while Git traffic grew exponentially, 99.99999% of the Git repositories on GitHub began living in two places at once: our own data centers and Azure. The rest are among the busiest on the platform, and they’re held back by just one thing: a 25ms round trip.
In an earlier blog post, we laid out the two principles behind our next-generation storage architecture:
- Minimize coordination
- Decouple storage from compute
In this post, we’ll look at the immediate bridge between our old design and our new one. We’ll talk about how a change to the way our quorum serializes writes gets the busiest repositories into Azure, and how that same step opens the door to replicas that keep no persistent state of their own.
How we got here
The timing and shape of the move were driven by the agentic shift: rapidly growing traffic, a hard ceiling on the power capacity of our data centers and the surrounding geographical region, and physical supply chain constraints. At the beginning of our migration, the remaining capacity with all possible expansion gave us enough time to migrate safely, but not enough to do it slowly.

articles.title: De una serie de YouTube a un juego viral: el título que está regalando Steam
articles.summary:
Steam ofrece de forma gratuita y permanente Heartfall - a Tale in Three Lives, un videojuego que surgió como proyecto creado por fanáticos de la serie de YouTube 3rd Life y que logró una calificación positiva del 99% entre sus jugadores. El título, no tiene fecha límite de reclamo y permanece en la biblioteca de quien lo agregue a su cuenta.
El fenómeno resulta llamativo porque combina el formato de las novelas visuales con un origen poco habitual: una producción audiovisual de YouTube transformada en una historia jugable mediante la colaboración de setenta personas. El resultado, desarrollado por Kazehita, se convirtió en una de las propuestas gratuitas con mejor recepción dentro de su comunidad en los últimos meses.
Un fangame construido en siete meses por setenta colaboradores
Heartfall nació como un proyecto colaborativo inspirado en 3rd Life, una serie disponible en YouTube con un grupo numeroso de seguidores. Su desarrollo reunió a setenta colaboradores, quienes trabajaron durante siete meses para dar forma a la historia, las ilustraciones y la música del juego.
El resultado final incluye más de 400.000 palabras de diálogo, más de 450 ilustraciones distribuidas a lo largo de la trama y más de 50 temas musicales originales. Esa cantidad de contenido permite recorrer distintos caminos narrativos, ya que la historia contempla varios finales posibles según las decisiones que tome el jugador.

articles.title: Big Tech’s thirst for water is sparking a global resistance
articles.summary:
After ChatGPT was released in November 2022, the tech industry was quick to herald the chatbot as the marker of a new wave of technological progress. As companies pushed to create more powerful AI models, the water demand of their ambitions took a while to become clear. In April 2023, a research paper out of the University of California estimated that training the large language model behind the initial version of ChatGPT had required 185,000 gallons of water. For every extended conversation someone had with the chatbot or every time they asked it to write an email, they were effectively pouring a bottle of water down the drain.
That statistic got a lot of play when it was released. It became an early warning sign of what was coming as companies pushed chatbots as a universal technology that could replace psychologists, educators, lawyers, and even people’s friends or partners.
As public concern grew, Google and OpenAI came out with their own figures. The companies suggested that querying one of their chatbots used mere drops of water. Independent researchers were not impressed, arguing the companies were taking a narrow view of the water use necessary to power and cool increasingly monstrous data centers. Those water demands can be quite significant too.

articles.title: Cleaning up PFAS
articles.summary:
Cleaning up PFAS
Ridding the world of forever chemicals could address a range of health and environmental and health woes.
Scrubbing Earth of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances—a.k.a. PFAS or forever chemicals—could eliminate a list of woes for people and planet. Used for decades in everything from nonstick pans to firefighting foams, PFAS have been linked to increased risks of fertility challenges, developmental delays, cancer, and reduced immune response. They are known for a strong bond between carbon and fluorine, which the environment struggles to break down.
The sticking points
PFAS are everywhere: They spew from factories and slough off products and into water with normal use. Scientists have found them in everything from human blood to Antarctic snow. One 2022 report found that 89% of the US population had PFAS in excess of two nanograms per milliliter of blood plasma, a common threshold for potential adverse health effects, and 9% of the population had passed the riskier level of 20 nanograms per milliliter.
The PFAS monster is also a moving target. New compounds are still being created and used. There are more than 12,000 of them, and much of the cleanup research focuses on only a small handful.

articles.summary:
Meta says it’s issuing a new class of shares to fund its AI initiatives. As part of its third-quarter earnings report released on Wednesday, the company says the non-voting stock will also go toward potential acquisitions and employee compensation, with trading beginning in 2027.
Meta to create a new class of shares to fund AI push
Meta says the new class of shares will also fund acquisitions and employee compensation.
“The scale of investment required to compete, sustain growth, expand infrastructure, and pursue new strategic initiatives amidst the AI transformation taking place in the industry is significant,” Meta says in the press release. Susan Li, Meta’s chief financial officer, added during an earnings call that the new class of shares will “expand our funding tools and give us flexibility to invest behind the unprecedented momentum we’re seeing across every part of our business driven by AI.”
Meta has poured billions of dollars into the AI race as it builds (and promotes) sprawling data centers, poaches top talent from other companies like OpenAI, and builds AI models capable of rivaling those from other tech giants. The company expects capital expenditures between $135 billion and $145 billion this year, up from the previous $130 billion and $145 billion estimate.

articles.title: Foursquare co-founder says equity holders saw no returns from the company's acquisition | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Last month, advertising company Infillion acquired location-data platform Foursquare, a once popular social network, at an undisclosed value. Now, in a new blog post, Foursquare co-founder and former CEO Dennis Crowley said that investors didn’t see any returns from the sale.
Crowley referenced a post by an angel investor, inferred that neither preferred nor common stockholders got any value out of the deal, and said he was disappointed by the outcome.
“I was heartbroken by this ending. So many people put so much time and energy and passion and love into building Foursquare — the company, the products, the brand, the culture. If you were part of it (or even close to it), you know exactly what I’m talking about. To our ~1600 former employees over 17 years, I am sorry the Foursquare story ended in such a way that makes it seem like our collective efforts were worth … nothing?” he said in the post.
Crowley said that the company did well after it started focusing on enterprise business and had consecutive years with over $100 million in revenue. In 2019, the company raised capital from a private equity firm and in 2021 brought in the banker who led the raise as CEO. Crowley blamed the final outcome on that transition, saying that the management of the company wasn’t able to preserve or create new value.
Foursquare, which had raised over $411 million in funding according to PitchBook data, eventually shut down its app in 2024.

articles.title: ‘Context Bombs’ Cut AI Attack Success by Misleading Agents With Fake Targets
articles.summary:
London- and New York-based Tracebit has developed a military style solution to AI attacks. Just as landmines are used to destroy or slow an advancing army, Tracebit has developed AI ‘context bombs’ that are planted in the battlefield. Each bomb comprises crafted and hidden prompts that are automatically ingested by the attacking AI when it crawls the target. These new prompts interfere with the original, possibly malign, purpose of the attacking agent.
Tracebit’s new research (Making attacking agents pay’) extends earlier research that used different context bombs to trigger guardrails. It now focuses on misdirecting and entrapping the agents with fake targets and deceptively complex problems. To achieve this, Tracebit developed nine new context techniques (ingested fake prompts) that stopped all GPT 5.6 Cyber, Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8 Max, and DeepSeek V4 Pro attacks. The same bombs also worked against Frontier Models, cutting GPT-6 Astra’s successes by 54% and nearly quadrupling its bill per attack. The effect against Claude Opus 5 was even more obvious: attack success was cut by 91%.
The single most effective of the nine prompt bombs was a fake pen testing report. It presented itself as a recent assessment, labeled real attack paths as canaries, and described decoys as valuable targets that had already been exploited. In many cases it made the AI believe the defender’s real systems were traps – so it avoided them, reducing the achieved objectives by 58%. Some agents accepted the …

articles.title: Electronic Arts cerrará BioWare y cancelará el próximo "Mass Effect" en un recorte de 400 empleos
articles.summary:
Electronic Arts anunció el cierre de BioWare, el estudio detrás de Mass Effect y Dragon Age, y la cancelación del próximo juego de esa franquicia. La medida forma parte de un recorte de unos 400 empleos, el 3% de su plantilla global.
La decisión quedó plasmada en una carta interna enviada a los empleados y firmada por Cam Weber, presidente y director de estudios, y David Tinson, presidente y director de operaciones. Según una persona con conocimiento del plan citada por Bloomberg, unos 50 de los despidos corresponden a BioWare, cuya oficina en Edmonton, Canadá, cerrará por completo.
“BioWare es un estudio legendario que ayudó a definir el género de rol, y no tomamos esta decisión a la ligera”, escribieron Weber y Tinson en la carta, según reprodujo la revista Variety. Los ejecutivos explicaron que un pequeño equipo de BioWare trabajaba en las primeras etapas de un nuevo Mass Effect, y que la empresa decidió no continuar ese desarrollo.
BioWare confirmó el cierre en un comunicado publicado en su cuenta oficial de X. “Después de más de tres décadas de aventuras compartidas, BioWare está cerrando y el desarrollo temprano del próximo proyecto de Mass Effect está terminando”, escribió el estudio. “No hay nada fácil en escribir esas palabras”, agregó, y dijo que su prioridad es acompañar a los empleados afectados.

C’est via un communiqué brutal, le 21 octobre 2026, qu’on a appris la disparition pure et simple de BioWare qui n’était déjà plus que l’ombre de lui-même ces dernières années. Le studio canadien est la grande victime de la réduction des coûts opérée par Electronic Arts, qui doit maintenant rendre des comptes à un consortium mené par le fonds souverain saoudien PIF.
BioWare aura quand même connu de sacrées heures de gloire, inscrivant une empreinte indélébile dans le genre du RPG occidental. Il laissera derrière lui un héritage en or massif, avec quelques pépites qui méritent encore tout notre temps aujourd’hui. Voici une sélection de 5 titres qui rendent hommage au savoir-faire du studio.
Cinq jeux pour rendre BioWare éternel
Trilogie Mass Effect
Il est difficile de ne choisir qu’un jeu de la trilogie Mass Effect (2007-2012), puisqu’elle forme une seule grande épopée à la narration poussée. Articulée autour d’un personnage charismatique, le commandant Shepard, plongé dans une guerre galactique, la saga est la définition même du space opera, comparable à des œuvres massives comme Star Wars. Alors oui, la fin initiale, qui ne respectait pas les choix censés être cruciaux des joueuses et des joueurs, en a déçu plus d’un, au point que BioWare a dû publier sous la pression une version étendue, l’Extended Cut, en 2012. Mais Mass Effect demeure une trilogie particulièrement marquante.

articles.title: Panne nationale chez Orange : 8 heures après les premières coupures, que sait-on de plus ?
articles.summary:
Plus de huit heures après les premières coupures ce mercredi 21 octobre, la panne mobile d’Orange et de Sosh se prolonge. L’opérateur confirme un incident national perturbant les appels, les SMS et les données mobiles d’une partie de ses clients. Le rétablissement complet des services reste attendu.
Le réseau revient chez certains abonnés, tandis que d’autres restent privés de service. Depuis les premières coupures signalées en fin de matinée, Orange a précisé l’ampleur des perturbations. Le constat dépasse désormais les seuls témoignages : l’opérateur reconnaît un incident national, sans avoir encore expliqué publiquement son origine.
Mise à jour du 21/10 à 19h30 : selon les informations de Numerama, la panne pourrait provenir d’une migration ratée d’une partie des abonnés vers un cœur de réseau 5G. La remise en cohérence des profils des lignes concernées compliquerait le rétablissement des services. Orange n’a pas confirmé cette explication dans sa réponse au média.
De son côté, RTL évoquait dans son dernier point qu'un retour à la normale serait envisagé autour de 21 heures, sous réserve de l’évolution de la panne. Cet horaire reste évidemment une estimation et aucun engagement officiel de l’opérateur n'a été communiqué. 
De nombreux lecteurs et lectrices nous ont fait savoir que le réseau était revenu pour eux, chez Sosh comme chez Orange. Ces premiers constats ne permettent toutefois pas encore de confirmer un rétablissement complet pour l'ensemble des clients.

articles.title: Interspecies communication
articles.summary:
Interspecies communication
Decoding how animals communicate could reveal the inner lives of other species—and give humans a window onto how they see the world.
Humans are far from the only species with a gift for gab, and our furry, feathered, and finned friends could have a lot to tell us. Decoding how animals communicate with one another could offer a window into the inner lives of other species and help humans realize that “animals are sentient creatures who think, who have hopes and dreams of their own,” says Con Slobodchikoff, the founder of Zoolingua, a company working on dog-to-human speech.
The sticking points
Teasing all this out is complex. To decipher howls, squeaks, and clicks, researchers must match the creatures making sounds with what’s happening around them. Prairie dogs, for example, utter a different series of yips when a coyote approaches than when a hawk is nearby. It’s painstaking work, especially for difficult-to-observe species, like deep-diving whales or subterranean mole rats.
There are other hurdles. Many animals communicate not just through sound but through visual cues, touch, pheromones, or a combination of signals, some of which might be difficult for us to perceive. And without a multispecies Rosetta stone, it’s hard to know if translations are accurate.
The progress

articles.summary:

Que ce soit pour du renseignement ou simplement pour faire peur, ces événements inquiètent toujours les autorités. Cette fois-ci, ce sont plusieurs survols sur des bases militaires du Var qui ont été repérés.
« Des gros engins » au-dessus de plusieurs bases militaires dans le Var
C’est ICI Provence qui a révélé que l’exercice militaire Typhon a été perturbé « par des survols non autorisés » au-dessus du site de la Direction Générale de l’Armement à Toulon, le 54e régiment d’artillerie à Hyères ou encore la base navale de Toulon. Les faits ce sont produits entre le 9 et le 13 octobre derniers.
La préfecture maritime de Toulon en est sûre : ces drones qui ont survolés tous ces sites sont sans lien avec cet exercice Typhon, qui prévoyait des manœuvres aériennes pour protéger tous ces sites en cas d’intrusion. Elle précise qu’aucune infrastructure sensible n’a été menacée. Tous les survols se sont déroulés dans la zone LF-P62 Toulon, une zone aérienne où les activités aériennes sont totalement interdites (sauf les opérations militaires et les urgences de sécurité civile).

articles.title: Achieve Productive AI Capacity Faster and More Predictably with NVIDIA DSX POD | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
AI factories turn energy into intelligence. But before an AI workload can produce its first token, operators must bring an interconnected system of compute, networking, storage, power, cooling, and software online as one productive unit.
In a conventional data center build, teams must first select the site, design power and cooling for the deployment, lay out the data center, and plan and install racks and cables. Then they can validate the network and cluster incrementally and bring service online. This work requires coordinated specialized labor, with critical dependencies among installation, infrastructure readiness, and system testing. Delays can push back bring-up and the date the infrastructure begins producing tokens.
NVIDIA DSX POD shifts more of this work into a controlled factory environment. One of multiple AI factory implementation models supported by NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, NVIDIA DSX POD reference design is the standardized, factory-built implementation. It enables partners to build standardized containers that pre-integrate AI infrastructure, complete critical validation before shipment, and connect to prepared site infrastructure after delivery. The result is a repeatable approach designed to reduce onsite integration complexity and help operators reach productive AI capacity faster and more predictably.

articles.title: Séisme près de Clermont-Ferrand : pourquoi une secousse de magnitude 3,6 s'est autant fait sentir
articles.summary:
En France métropolitaine, les tremblements de terre sont rares, mais ils peuvent tout de même se produire. Cette fois, c’est le Puy-de-Dôme qui a été touché avec un séisme mesuré à une magnitude de 3,6, à quelques kilomètres à l’est de Clermont-Ferrand.
Selon le Réseau National de Surveillance Sismique (RENASS), le tremblement de terre a eu lieu dans la nuit du 21 au 22 octobre 2026, aux alentours de 4 heures du matin et l’épicentre serait localisé du côté de la ville d’Ambert, toujours dans le Puy-de-Dôme. Au départ évalué à 13 kilomètres de profondeur, le séisme aurait finalement, d’après des analyses plus poussées, eu lieu vers 10 kilomètres sous la terre seulement. Une profondeur assez faible, qui explique qu’il a pu être davantage ressenti que d’autres tremblements de terre aussi puissants, mais qui ont lieu plus profondément.
Des séismes habituellement rares et faibles dans le Massif central
Le Massif central fait partie des zones françaises considérées comme étant à risque modéré en ce qui concerne les séismes. Les Pyrénées ou les Alpes notamment, ainsi que le sud du massif des Vosges, connaissent de leur côté un risque plus élevé. Il n’est ainsi pas rare que des séismes se déclenchent dans les environs de Clermont-Ferrand, mais une magnitude aussi élevée est tout de même assez peu fréquente.

articles.title: Waymo starts offering rides at the Las Vegas airport | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Waymo is now shuttling customers to and from the Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas, with pickups and drop-offs happening at dedicated “autonomous vehicle zones” at Terminal 1 and Terminal 3, the company announced Wednesday.
This is the sixth major airport that Waymo is serving. The company already offers rides at Phoenix Sky Harbor, Nashville International, San Antonio International, San Francisco International, and San José International airports.
Waymo only just started offering rides to the public in Las Vegas in September but is already serving a 24-square-mile area in the city. The company said the rides to and from the Las Vegas airport will be limited at first to just a few riders, before opening up to all customers.
Amazon-owned Zoox already offers rides at the Vegas airport, and more robotaxis are coming to Sin City. In August, state regulators approved permits that will allow Tesla and Uber to put thousands of them on the city’s streets in the next year.

articles.title: Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains
articles.summary:
A rush of new data centers could bring air pollution roaring back to levels not seen since the 2000s in Texas, which has become ground zero for the physical infrastructure behind generative AI.
Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains
New research out of Texas shows how data centers are driving up pollution.
New and proposed data centers are demanding a tremendous amount of electricity. How developers and utilities meet that demand — with gas turbines or renewable energy — will determine just how dirty things will get. So far, though, things are looking grim.
Tech companies and data center developers are devising new ways to get enough electricity, including building out their own power sources. But if all planned data center projects were to plug into the electricity grid in Texas and be powered by the anticipated grid mix, soot and smog-forming pollutants would skyrocket, according to a new report from the Houston Advanced Research Center (HARC). In just five years, it would be enough pollution to wipe out decades of gains in air quality.
“There is a good chance that our children and grandchildren will breathe dirtier air than we did.”
In that scenario, fine particle pollution or soot from the power sector would more than triple, reaching its highest level since 2006. articles.title: How Commerce.com and Cloudflare are getting storefronts ready for AI agents
articles.summary:
How Commerce.com and Cloudflare are getting storefronts ready for AI agents
AI can write code and pass the bar exam, but it still struggles to buy a pair of shoes online.
That’s because websites were built for humans, not agents. Most agents that shop for someone today work from a site’s HTML — they look at the page, guess which button does what, click, and try again when they get it wrong. This process is slow, uses a lot of tokens, and something as seemingly innocuous as a theme change can break it.
Enter WebMCP: a browser standard from Google that gives AI agents structured tools on a page, like search_products. Instead of hunting for buttons, the agent calls the exact tool it needs directly, making shopping faster, cheaper, and far more reliable. Because WebMCP is still an experimental proposed browser standard in early preview, it’s currently available behind experimental Chrome flags (chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing), in Chrome Origin Trials, in some agentic browsers, and across developer environments like Cloudflare Kitesurf.

articles.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
articles.summary:
Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: PHP2Shell Patches Land as First Exploitation Attempts Hit Sensors
articles.summary:
PHP has rolled out patches for two critical-severity vulnerabilities named PHP2Shell that could provide attackers with unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE).
The issues are tracked as CVE-2026-109618 (out-of-memory (OOM) corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (stale global state) and have a CVSS score of 9.2. For both, RCE was confirmed on Apache with mod_php.
“Both issues sit in parts of PHP that nearly every request touches: memory management and error handling. Their central place in PHP is what made both vulnerabilities serious, and also so hard to fix,” the PHP Foundation says.
Patches for both were included in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, PHP 8.0, and PHP 8.1 were also released.
Before the fixes arrived, however, proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits targeting the two security defects started circulating.
Preemptive attack surface management firm WatchTowr says it has seen the first in-the-wild exploitation attempts hitting its sensors around the same time the patches landed, but has not observed successful attempts.
“Whilst nobody has been successful to date, we don’t expect that will last long,” WatchTowr head of threat intelligence Jake Knott said.
Several other companies reported seeing exploitation attempts, including before the patches landed.

articles.title: Colonizar Marte nos va a romper literalmente el corazón
articles.summary:
La conquista de Marte es el próximo gran salto de la exploración espacial, pero el cuerpo humano no ha evolucionado lo suficiente para sobrevivir en el espacio profundo. Esto es un grave problema, puesto que nos exige tener tecnología puntera para enviar una tripulación al planeta rojo, pero también hay un cuello de botella biológico.
El otro peligro. Históricamente, la principal preocupación médica ha sido el riesgo de cáncer por la exposición a la radiación cósmica. Sin embargo, un nuevo estudio financiado por la NASA ha puesto el foco en otro órgano vital como es el corazón.
Esta investigación ha analizado cómo los estresores de los vuelos espaciales afectan a nivel cardiovascular, y para ello se ha sometido a un grupo de ratas a una combinación de descarga de las patas traseras, simulando los efectos de la microgravedad, y a ráfagas de iones pesados que emulan los rayos cósmicos que nos encontramos en el espacio. Todo esto, obviamente, en un simulador especializado.
El resultado que presenciaron fue que la radiación indujo fibrosis perivascular que es un engrosamiento y endurecimiento del tejido que hay alrededor de los vasos sanguíneos del corazón. Algo que puede dificultar mucho que pueda hacer su trabajo correctamente y distribuya la sangre por todo el organismo.
Pero lo más preocupante es que esta fibrosis no aparece de manera instantánea, sino que se hace visible muchos meses después de la exposición a estas condiciones. Y para que nos hagamos una idea, con una dosis…

articles.title: Exercise in a pill
articles.summary:
Exercise in a pill
In unraveling the pathways by which movement helps the body, we could develop medicines that offer some of the same benefits, without the workout.
We all know exercise is good for us. It builds muscle, strengthens bones, lowers blood pressure, and boosts mood. By deciphering how movement benefits the body, researchers hope to develop medicines that can offer some of the same perks—without the workout. The idea isn’t to replace exercise but to bring its upsides to people who struggle with frailty, disability, or chronic illness.
The sticking points
It will take a lot of experimentation to untangle the myriad pathways by which exercise promotes health. But IDing the cascade of hormones, enzymes, and other molecules related to physical activity is just the first step. Scientists need to figure out how to turn that knowledge into safe and effective drugs. That’s a tall order: More than 90% of treatments that enter human studies fail.
There are regulatory hurdles too. The FDA approves medications to treat diseases, not to enhance wellness, says Thomas Burris, a pharmacologist at the University of Florida whose work focuses on diseases that respond to exercise, like obesity, type 2 diabetes, and dementia.
The progress
There may never be a pill that delivers all the benefits of exercise, but research could lead to new medicines that mimic some aspects of working out. Scientists have already identified many important exercise-related signals and have even developed…

When the cleanup began, AI writing was often betrayed by conspicuous clichés. Today, the project’s volunteers are developing tools to detect subtler forms of machine-generated content and debating AI’s role in the world’s most widely used encyclopedia.
When did you realize Wikipedia had a problem with AI-generated material?
Ellia Lebleu: It was around December 2023. A few other editors and I were chatting on Wikipedia’s Discord server, and we had all seen very strange articles with the same odd characteristics. They repeated phrases like “stands as a testament” or “rich cultural heritage.” They sometimes had conclusion sections, or sections called “Why is this important?” That was very typical of ChatGPT in 2023 and early 2024 but very odd for Wikipedia articles—and very easy to spot. Then I decided, let’s create an official project on Wikipedia so more people can deal with this.

Actor-theatre artist Prakash Belawadi began his session at TechSparks 2026 with a simple question: “Any artists out there?”

articles.title: Solving a 31-year-old grand challenge in mathematics – the KLS conjecture - Microsoft Research
articles.summary:
Microsoft researcher and collaborator combine new mathematical ideas with human-directed AI to resolve a central problem in high-dimensional geometry and probability
At a glance
- Fundamental scientific breakthrough: Researchers resolved the Kannan-Lovász-Simonovits (KLS) conjecture, a 31-year-old problem widely regarded as one of the central open questions in high-dimensional geometry, with implications for statistics, optimization, algorithms, and computer science.
- A universal geometric principle: The result establishes a universal geometric principle for log-concave distributions, showing that simple flat cuts can capture their narrowest bottlenecks within a fixed factor, regardless of dimension.
- Human-AI collaboration: The breakthrough emerged from a human-directed agentic research process in which AI systems explored mathematical possibilities while researchers evaluated, pruned, and redirected the search.

The U.S. National Security Agency’s sent out an alarming warning on Wednesday that two critical holes had been found in PHP, with patches already issued by the PHP Foundation.
PHP is a server-side programming language so widely used for web applications that it powers roughly 70% of the websites on the internet; by some accounts, that’s more than 33 million sites. It is also used by popular content management systems like WordPress.

Websites not running relatively current versions of PHP will have some updating work to do, as PHP 8.1 and older versions are no longer supported. The recommendation is to update the web server to the current version of PHP, which is 8.5.12.

A new era of spaceflight could save astronauts time and cut exposure to cosmic radiation as they rocket to Mars—and beyond.
Just before the Artemis II crew began its historic slingshot around the moon this past April, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom. SR-1, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-powered interplanetary spacecraft, is meant to fly an uncrewed mission to Mars by the end of 2028, arriving in 2029. A successful mission would herald a new era of more efficient, potentially faster spaceflight—saving astronauts time and cutting their exposure to harmful cosmic radiation as they travel to Mars and beyond. “You wake up to that announcement, and it puts a big smile on your face,” says Simon Middleburgh, co-director of the Nuclear Futures Institute at Bangor University in Wales.

articles.title: Getting old is hard. This age-tech housing aims to make it easier. | BetaKit
articles.summary:
My grandmother was a commanding woman. In her 92 years, she raised three children and a grandchild, mostly by herself. She helped manage a series of successful restaurants and nightclubs; in her little spare time, she hiked and skied. She was decidedly capable.
But when I unexpectedly knocked on her door one autumn when I was 19, something was different: she asked me the same questions, different only in sentence structure, again and again.
What brought me to town?
Where was I going to school?
What was I doing in town?
What college was I enrolled in?
Over the years, she lost more of her faculties. Eventually, she left the stovetop on for so long that a steel pot melted into molten coagulant. That was the boiling point: a week later she moved in with my parents.
My grandmother’s experience was not abnormal. Like many seniors, she was caught between her desire to remain independent and the limitations of her advancing age; she didn’t want to leave her home, but could also no longer live safely on her own. With little money to afford in-home care, those years put untold pressure on my parents and left my grandmother in a sort of purgatory: she wasn’t independent, but she also didn’t have round-the-clock care.
If Calgary’s Garden Loft had been around back then, might things have been different?

TornadoVM, an open-source heterogeneous GPU programming framework for Java has reached version 7.3, a major milestone for the project.
InfoQ previously covered the project in December 2025 and in 2022.
TornadoVM automatically accelerates Java programs on multi-core CPUs and GPUs. Rather than replacing existing JVMs, it works alongside them and provides a rich GPU programming ecosystem in Java that you can use with any mainstream JDK distribution such as OpenJDK, Graalvm, Temurin, or Zulu.
It offloads Java code to hardware backends, manages memory between the Java heap and accelerators, and runs the resulting compute kernels. This makes it a useful building block for modern cloud and machine learning workloads.
During development, TornadoVM compiles the source Java code to OpenCL and Apple Metal backends. The idea is that you can develop locally on your laptop and use the hardware available locally, and then deploy into a server that has Nvidia GPUs, and achieve major performance improvements - a form of "Write Once, Run Anywhere" for modern ML workloads.
Version 7 brings several architectural changes. The backends now use the Foreign Function & Memory (FFM) API in place of the Java Native Interface (JNI). The experimental JVM Compiler Interface (JVMCI) dependency has also been removed. According to the team, TornadoVM now sources "all compiler metadata through a reflection + ASM + Unsafe layer" which is the single, uniform path on every supported JDK (21, 25, 26 and 27).

De momento no se ha encontrado nada infalible; pero, según un nuevo estudio, un fármaco de la familia de la Viagra podría ser bastante útil.
Ojo: solo en células de ratón. Este estudio no se ha llevado a cabo en humanos. Ni siquiera en animales de laboratorio vivos. El fármaco en cuestión se ha probado sobre células de ratón cultivadas en laboratorio. Sus autores, un equipo de científicos de la Universidad de Roma, optaron por probar el tadalafilo, un medicamento de la misma familia de compuestos que el sildenafilo, más conocido como Viagra. The Gemini and ClickFix protections are part of Enhanced Protection, the Safe Browsing mode Google introduced in 2020. Last year, the company said more than 1 billion Chrome users had turned it on.
Google claims Enhanced Protection makes users “ten times safer” than Standard Protection against phishing, social engineering, notification abuse, and other scams. The metric is based on how many safety warnings, on average, each group of users receives.
Chrome’s Safe Browsing site warnings now come in two levels, mirroring a model previously applied to file downloads. When Safe Browsing is highly confident a page is malicious, users still get the full-page red ‘dangerous site’ warning.
The new ‘suspicious site’ level covers lower-confidence verdicts. It flags pages that use deceptive tactics typical of known malicious sites. Because these warnings have their own design, Google says it can safely display more of them.
Gemini-powered scam detection has also moved to Google’s servers. The on-device version launched last year focused on tech support scams and was limited to Enhanced Protection users on supported devices.
The more capable server-side model is now available to every Enhanced Protection user. It also targets additional threats, such as fake antivirus and fake browser update pages.

From backup to energy management: how batteries are changing India's power needs
As electricity demand rises and renewable energy adoption expands, batteries are evolving from backup devices into critical tools for businesses to manage energy use, improve reliability, and build more resilient power systems.
For years, the conversation around batteries in Indian businesses was fairly straightforward: How much backup do you need?
That question is changing.
In conversations with businesses, channel partners, and people working across the energy ecosystem, I have increasingly noticed that the discussion is moving beyond backup duration. Businesses are asking how they can manage their energy better, protect critical operations, integrate renewable power and reduce their dependence on a single source of electricity.

articles.title: YouTube says it isn’t testing hiding the dislike button
articles.summary:
On Tuesday, I published a story about how YouTube appeared to be testing hiding the dislike button on videos, with at least two users on X sharing screenshots of the dislike button moved into the three-dot menu. But a YouTube spokesperson, in a Wednesday statement to The Verge, confirmed that YouTube is “not testing hiding the dislike button on YouTube for users.”
YouTube says it isn’t testing hiding the dislike button
YouTube creators, on their own videos, will have the dislike button moved behind the three-dot menu, but that’s not the case for regular users.
However, YouTube is introducing a new UI for creators on their uploaded videos where the dislike button will be moved.
Here’s the full statement, from spokesperson Kimberly Taylor:
We are not testing hiding the dislike button on YouTube for users. We’re introducing a new UI for creators on their own uploaded videos, where dislike is behind the three-dot menu, and as always, they can find their full dislike counts in Studio, alongside other analytics.
The new UI is rolling out to creators in “the coming weeks,” Taylor says.
The change for creators follows past adjustments to the dislike button on the platform. YouTube hid the public dislike count on videos starting in 2021 as a way to prevent harassment, and it removed the dislike button video from Shorts earlier this year.
Update, October 21st: Added context about the UI rollout timing from Taylor.

Avec Clarence Cloud, cette approche prend une nouvelle dimension, jusqu’à permettre l’utilisation de l’intelligence artificielle dans un environnement isolé.
Aujourd’hui, le cloud est devenu tellement incontournable qu’on en oublie parfois ce qu’il implique, et notamment confier ses données, ses applications et une partie de son infrastructure informatique à un prestataire extérieur. Pour une entreprise, une administration, un acteur stratégique ou un simple particulier, cette dépendance peut soulever des questions bien concrètes. Que se passe-t-il lorsque les données hébergées sont particulièrement sensibles ? Comment s’assurer qu’elles restent protégées face aux cyberattaques, mais aussi aux législations étrangères ?
Une question d’autant plus importante quand on voit à quel point les attaques informatiques se multiplient et que les fuites de données continuent de faire la une de l’actualité. Dans ce contexte, des acteurs comme Clarence Cloud explorent une approche radicale, celle de conserver les avantages du cloud… tout en supprimant sa connexion à Internet.
Souveraineté numérique : pourquoi l’Europe doit-elle protéger ses données ?

Complex engineering feats — from advanced chips to aircraft to industrial systems —– depend on simulation to predict how designs will perform before they’re built. As designs become more complex, simulations take longer to run, increasing computing demands and limiting the number of ideas teams can test.
NVIDIA cuDSS accelerates solving large sparse systems — the math-heavy step that repeats throughout engineering and scientific simulations and often limits how many designs a team can test — by tapping into GPUs. - Joomla 6.2.0

articles.title: Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF
articles.summary:
Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF
Today, we are expanding our web application firewall (WAF) by adding two new capabilities: full transaction detections and response rules. Full transaction detections evaluate each HTTP request alongside its response to identify evidence of exploitation. It helps answer both "Does this request look malicious?" and "What happened when the application handled it?" Response rules can then block the origin’s response before it reaches the requester.
These are valuable protections because the latest frontier models are uncovering vulnerabilities buried deep in widely used software, giving defenders clarity on what to fix — and attackers new paths to exploit. The recent php2shell vulnerability shows the stakes: a flaw in a common software component can put applications across the Internet at risk. AI agents scanning for vulnerabilities can be extremely persistent, adapting payloads using feedback, and chaining vulnerabilities, credentials, and permissions. An application's response can reveal whether an attempt worked and give an attacker information that helps them go deeper.
Inspecting incoming requests remains essential for stopping recognizable attacks before they reach an application. But some threats become clear only when the request is considered alongside what the origin returns. A suspicious input followed by a response exposing sensitive information tells a different story from the same input followed by a rejecti…

The design, as described in the announcement, tracks intent instead of versions. A developer asks for a channel such as latest, lts, preview, daily, a major like 10, a minor like 10.0, or a feature band like 10.0.1xx, and dotnetup resolves it to a release. Exact versions, as the post notes, stay pinned during updates.
Several requirements can share one managed installation, and the tool reads the nearest global.json so team builds stay deterministic. Furthermore, according to the docs, files live under the user's local data directory on Windows, macOS, and Linux, and dotnetup never writes to Program Files\dotnet or /usr/share/dotnet.
Installation uses a bootstrap script fetched from aka.ms with curl or irm. articles.title: Inside NVIDIA Sentry: Secure AI Agents at Runtime | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
An AI agent can complete its assignment and still cross a security boundary. Recent incidents show that agents can circumvent security controls while using tools, credentials, and services to pursue their assigned goals. Monitoring and enforcement need to operate outside the agent’s reach so that it can’t alter or disable them.
NVIDIA Sentry is a security software framework that monitors AI agents and enforces policies governing their access to models, tools, and data. Part of the NVIDIA OpenShell reference architecture announced at GTC Berlin, it’s built on NVIDIA DOCA, runs on NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs, and provides host-isolated runtime protection for AI agents. NVIDIA Sentry validates that an agent operates according to its designed intent and within its defined operational boundaries.
Trusted even when host resources can’t be trusted, it controls the agent’s only path to the model, providing tamper-evident traceability of agent activity while enforcing granular security controls on agent access in silicon. In addition to inspecting agent communications, NVIDIA Sentry uses out-of-band observability to establish real-time situational awareness, continuously evaluating agents’ runtime security and behavior to validate their security and integrity.
This post explains how NVIDIA Sentry evaluates agent requests, detects threats, and enforces security policies independently of host software.

Always On VPN replaced the legacy DirectAccess technology and supports domain-joined, non-domain-joined, and Microsoft Entra ID–joined devices running Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server.
It runs in the background and establishes secure tunnels back to the user's corporate network whenever their device connects to the internet.
Microsoft first acknowledged the issue in a service alert sent to IT administrators in late September, saying it was triggered on systems running Windows 11 24H2 and later after installing the September 2026 security updates when the initial Always On VPN connection failed (e.g., when using automatic protocol selection with IKEv2 and SSTP).
"When automatic protocol selection or protocol fallback was configured, affected VPN connections could remain stuck in a Connecting state or fail to connect after an initial connection attempt failed," it said. "In some cases, subsequent connection attempts could display the error, 'The specified port is already in use.'"
Mistakenly marked as resolved
After releasing the October 2026 Patch Tuesday Windows 11 cumulative updates, Microsoft marked the bug as resolved, but in a Tuesday update it said the issues weren't actually addressed and that a fix would ship later.

Advanced packaging growth and capacity constraints are pushing more onto OSATs.

Foundries and outsourced assembly and test (OSAT) houses have traditionally had distinct lanes, but the lines are blurring as OSATs acquire select foundry capabilities and foundries return some of the jobs they have taken from OSATs.
“We’re at this bridging point where the IDMs and the foundries are doing more of what OSATs can do, and the OSATs are also trying to get much closer to what the foundry does at the back end,” said Raghu Nayak, head of sales at Zeiss.
OSATs will never compete with foundries on advanced nodes and front-end wafer fabrication. But for backend activities, where dimensions aren’t as demanding, OSATs are acquiring capabilities that replicate what foundries can do. The biggest areas of overlap are 2.5D integration and panel assembly, with hybrid bonding likely to move there as well.
The change affects equipment and materials. “We are seeing the migration of lithography-related materials and processes from traditional wafer fabs into advanced packaging environments,” said Poupak Khodabandeh, chief business officer at Brewer Science. “As advanced packaging increasingly relies on fine-pitch redistribution layers (RDLs), OSATs and packaging organizations are using materials and process flows that historically would have been associated with wafer fabrication.”

articles.title: AI’s hidden storage bill: What inference leaves behind
articles.summary:
Sponsored
Provided byWD
Ask most executives to picture the cost of AI and they’ll likely see GPUs—racks of accelerators with gigawatts of power—and a waitlist for silicon. But that picture leaves something out: Data storage costs.
What happens to data after a model responds? Much of the back-end data that’s generated—from billions of daily prompts, images, and videos—needs to be stored. But data storage is one of the harder infrastructure costs to plan for, and it’s often overlooked in initial AI infrastructure planning.
As inference scales, the data footprint grows with it
Traditionally, AI infrastructure conversations have centered on the compute-intensive process of training a model. Training is finite: a run starts, burns through compute, and ends. But inference runs continuously, every time a model answers a prompt. For infrastructure planning, that difference matters: A training run is a project you can budget for and retire. Inference doesn’t retire; every inference request leaves something behind.
Take AI-generated video. In this workload, the back-end spend can be significant. From internal measurements, WD found that an 8-second clip (returned to a user as a 3.97MB 720p file) left more than 500MB of associated data behind on the back end, including logs, cached context, immediate renders, backups, and safety records. articles.title: Estudo encontra pista no DNA que pode explicar por que cães grandes vivem menos
articles.summary:
Cães de raças grandes podem envelhecer mais rápido por perderem parte do controle sobre trechos do DNA conhecidos como “genes saltadores”. É o que sugere um estudo publicado na revista Science.
A pesquisa analisou 864 cães e identificou uma perda mais acelerada de marcas químicas que regulam esses elementos genéticos nos animais de maior porte. O achado pode ajudar a investigar por que cães gigantes tendem a viver menos que os pequenos.
O que são os “genes saltadores”?
Os chamados genes saltadores são elementos transponíveis: trechos de DNA capazes de produzir cópias de si mesmos e inseri-las em outras regiões do genoma. Uma classe desses elementos, conhecida como LINE1, foi o foco da pesquisa.
O organismo controla a atividade desses trechos por meio da metilação, um processo que adiciona marcas químicas ao DNA sem alterar sua sequência. Com o envelhecimento, parte dessas marcas se perde, o que pode reduzir o controle sobre os LINE1. Quando ficam excessivamente ativos, esses elementos têm sido associados a danos no DNA, câncer e outras doenças relacionadas à idade.
“O que descobrimos é que a regulação epigenética dos elementos transponíveis, especialmente dos LINE1, parece ser um fator importante para determinar a velocidade com que diferentes cães envelhecem”, afirmou Noah Snyder-Mackler, autor sênior do estudo, em nota da Universidade Estadual do Arizona, nos Estados Unidos.

The third adds Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) mixture-of-experts (MoE) kernels from the torchtitan-neuron recipes and then uses torchtitan’s override registry to attach your own kernel. All three configurations use the same torchrun launch pattern and config structure.

articles.title: Cilium 1.20 Expands Gateway API and Opens eBPF Datapath for Kubernetes
articles.summary:
Cilium 1.20 has been released with broader Kubernetes Gateway API support, an extensible eBPF datapath and further work on sidecarless mutual TLS. The release also makes the newer netkit network device easier to introduce across Kubernetes fleets that run different Linux kernel versions.
In the release announcement, Cilium engineers Nico Vibert and Donia Chaiehloudj describe Gateway API as a "much broader traffic management layer" in version 1.20. Cilium moves from Gateway API 1.4 to 1.6, adding ExternalAuth, ListenerSets, CORS filtering, TCPRoute and UDPRoute. These additions bring HTTP authentication and non-HTTP services such as databases and DNS under the same Kubernetes API used for web and gRPC traffic.
According to Vibert and Chaiehloudj, ExternalAuth allows an HTTPRoute to consult an external authorisation service before sending a request to an application. Depending on the response, the gateway can forward the request, redirect a user to a login page, or reject it. The authoriser can also pass identity headers to the application. TCPRoute and UDPRoute remove the need to fall back to LoadBalancer or NodePort Services for plain Layer 4 traffic.
ListenerSets address a separate ownership problem. Application teams can add listeners from their own namespaces while a platform team retains control of the shared Gateway and decides which namespaces may extend it. Clément Delangue, cofondateur et patron français de l’entreprise, a démonté le résultat mardi dans un long message publié sur X.
 Just watched the @netflix Instadocs about the @OpenAI cyberattack on @huggingface. Super disappointing, as they went for maximum anthropomorphism of the technology and full doomer mode.
I spent more than two hours with them trying to correct all their mistakes and ground this in reality, explaining that agents are technological systems, not aliens. But it looks like the drive to scare people for maximum views was too strong.
Also, they didn’t mention the lack of containment and monitoring of the agents, how closed-model safeguards blocked our defensive work, or how we defended ourselves with AI using an open model. It ends up being a fun sci-fi movie though!

What’s in the box

The containers also come with roughly 20 kilometers of copper cabling and 17 kilometers of scale-out networking preinstalled and tested. Once a container arrives, crews set it in place, connect it to its neighbors, and run the final burn-in tests, Buck said.

Eight intermediate certificate authority keys linked to eMudhra’s global website-security business were found to be dangerously weak, raising concerns about the systems that browsers use to establish trust online.
The flaw could have enabled attackers to create fraudulent HTTPS certificates and impersonate legitimate websites. The keys were generated on April 30, 2025, but the weakness remained undetected for about 18 months, according to eMudhra’s statement on October 21, 2026.
A certificate authority (CA) verifies identities and issues digital certificates. Intermediate authorities operate under a root certificate trusted by browsers and operating systems.

Although the company added its root private key was not compromised, browser operators have withdrawn trust from the associated emSign ECC Root CA - G3 as a precaution.

articles.title: What Breaks When Packaging Moves From Wafer To Panel?
articles.summary:
Engineers are discovering many things they thought were process assumptions were actually wafer assumptions.
Key Takeaways:
Moving advanced packaging from wafer to panel sounds, at first, like a geometry problem. Large AI and HPC packages are increasingly rectangular, while the 300mm wafer underneath them is still round. As the package size grows, more of that expensive processing ends up around the circle’s edges where nothing useful can be built.
A panel gives that area back. It can fit more large packages into the same process cycle, and unlike a wafer, its dimensions don’t impose the same hard limit on the size of a square or rectangular package. For advanced packages that keep getting larger, the economics are difficult to ignore.
But the semiconductor packaging sector has spent decades learning how to process wafers, not panels. Equipment, materials, recipes, handling systems, and process controls were all developed around the geometry and mechanical behavior of a round workpiece.
“The risk of doing the assembly on the 600mm panel is high, and I don’t think we have all the equipment today to run the process,” said Teck Chong Lee, technical director of advanced fan-out development for HPC applications at ASE, in a recent presentation. “One of the options is, once you complete the interposer in large format in 600, then you divide it into four pieces to run the assembly and the C4 process. This is a much lower-risk approach.”

articles.summary:
Three things you should know about permafrost
A primer on this crucial and frankly mysterious piece of climate science.
How much do you know about permafrost?
Maybe, like me, you’ve been aware that this layer of frozen soil is thawing, that it’s important in the global puzzle of climate change … and that’s about the extent of it.
The great news for both of us is that my colleague James Temple just published two in-depth stories about permafrost. His reporting took him to the boreal forests of Alaska, where he helicoptered into the wilderness to learn more about how this material could affect our climate both now and in the future.
I’d recommend you give both of James’s stories a read. There’s this feature about efforts to tackle the intensifying fires that are threatening permafrost, as well as this look at how researchers are trying to understand the complicated tangle of potential climate effects. Here are three things I took away.
Permafrost is a massive blind spot for climate change
Permafrost is the frozen layer of soil that’s under about 15% of land around the Northern Hemisphere. While technically material needs to be frozen for only two consecutive years to count as permafrost, most of our current permafrost formed during the last ice age.

Vermieter auf der Unterkünfte-Plattform Airbnb dürfen von ihren Gästen nicht mehr verlangen, dass sie zum Check-out das Geschirr abwaschen und die Betten abziehen. Laut einer neuen Richtlinie für Hausregeln lässt Airbnb nur noch Aufgaben zu, die als «zumutbar» erachtet werden. Organizations building AI agents face a common challenge: Every request, whether a routine status check or complex analysis, typically gets routed to a single large, expensive model. This one-size-fits-all approach can drive up API costs, introduce unpredictable latency, and remove the possibility of offline operation. Even routine queries that could resolve locally end up requiring a full network round-trip to a cloud-hosted large language model (LLM).
The Adaptive Agentic Intelligence Framework (AAIF), built with Strands Agents, takes a different approach. Instead of routing all requests to a single large model, AAIF uses small language models (SLMs) to handle routine tasks locally. More complex requests are routed to cloud-hosted models through Amazon Bedrock. This approach builds on the research position from Belcak et al. at NVIDIA. They argue that small language models are “sufficiently powerful, inherently more suitable, and necessarily more economical for many invocations in agentic systems.” Built on Strands Agents, the framework demonstrates how intelligent model orchestration can help reduce costs while maintaining low latency for local operations.

By Kaladhar Radhakrishnan, Nicolas Butzen, and Vishal Javvaji
The semiconductor industry has embraced multi-chip and stacked-die architectures as the primary path for continued performance scaling. As monolithic designs become more difficult and costly to advance, chiplets, advanced packaging, and 3D integration enable higher levels of performance, bandwidth, and functional integration for AI and high-performance computing (HPC) systems.

articles.title: Distributed Spring Batch Without a Message Broker
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Spring Batch can scale horizontally without a message broker by using the relational database it already requires as the coordination plane. It fits the small-to-medium clusters many teams run.
- The pattern solves the problems a broker otherwise handles for you: sizing work to the live node count, assigning per-execution master responsibility with no standing coordinator, and claiming partitions with compare-and-set writes so no partition is silently lost.
- Node failure is handled by heartbeats and a two-phase recovery. It marks a stale node as unreachable, then after a grace period window, removes it and reassigns its incomplete, transferable partitions.
- Correctness is an explicit contract. Transferable work runs at least once and must be idempotent; nontransferable work runs at most once and is failed rather than moved. A partition is never silently lost.
- Database coordination fits where operational simplicity and cost matter most. Its ceiling is database contention and past that point, at very large clusters or sub-second latency, a broker remains the better choice.
Introduction
Spring Batch has been the default framework for batch processing on the JVM for more than a decade. Jobs are built from steps, such as chunk-oriented readers, processors, and writers, with a metadata repository that makes runs restartable. 5 production challenges in multi-agent systems and how Deep Insight solved them
Building a multi-agent system is now pretty straightforward. Taking it to production is where the real challenges begin. Thanks to open source frameworks and cloud services, you can set up an agent in a matter of days. A few tool calls, a few lines of prompt, and you have something that looks impressive. But the moment teams try to move beyond a pilot and into real business applications, they hit a familiar wall. If you’ve ever tried to put an agent into production, these frustrations will sound familiar:
Why doesn’t the agent follow our business logic, skip validation steps, or catch edge cases?
You tweak the prompt, add more examples, swap out the model. The same problems keep coming back. That’s because agents don’t follow a fixed sequence of instructions. They make their own judgments based on context. Instructions alone aren’t enough. You need to design how the agent thinks, when it verifies, and what it does when things go wrong. This is exactly why it’s become critical to go beyond prompt engineering alone and design the agent’s entire cognitive architecture and execution flow.

articles.title: ClickFix has never been bigger, and AI tools are its most convincing lure yet
articles.summary:
ClickFix has fast become one of the go-to techniques for criminals since it first emerged around 2024. It’s grown in both volume and variety, with an ever-expanding family of sub-techniques like FileFix, InstallFix, TerminalFix, and the entirely browser-native ConsentFix.
The lures too have become more developed and targeted, with recent attacks preferring to target people searching for and using AI tools, a trick that is catching many users off guard and blending in with otherwise legitimate traffic for approved GenAI tools.
Push's detection data shows how far the technique has spread. Through Q2 2026, ClickFix made up an average of 52% of Push's detections, overtaking AiTM and device code phishing for the first time, and in August that figure reached 67%.
Across all the browser-based attacks Push intercepts, 1 in 2 arrive through channels other than email, such as search engines and social media. The rest came through email but weren’t stopped at the email gateway. ClickFix goes a step further: 4 in 5 ClickFix pages intercepted in 2026 were reached from search engines — through compromised websites, malvertising, and SEO poisoning.
AI tools are the newest lure
The latest ClickFix variants use AI tools as the bait. In Push's last quarterly snapshot, AI-themed InstallFix and LLMshare attacks made up around 5% of all attacks Push detected, a growing subset of the ClickFix family.

Introduced by Council member Liliana Bakhtiari, the act prohibits city employees and contractors, including police, from buying or otherwise acquiring weaponized autonomous systems, drones and remotely operated machines.
In addition to drones, these autonomous killing machines include robot dogs and military-like robots armed with weapons. The act specifically exempts machines used strictly for neutralizing explosives.
"This is about making sure that we are investing in technology with our officers, not replacing them, quite frankly, with 'RoboCop,'" Bakhtiari said.
While we're still not in the era of ED-209 asking people to put down their weapons (then killing them even if they do), Bakhtiari believes the act is a pre-emptive step to ensure this doesn't happen.
The act is also there to stop AI-powered machines from replacing the decision-making of trained Atlanta Police officers. Letting AI make potentially lethal decisions in war is something that militaries have spent years saying would never happen, but that scenario seems closer than ever.

The PHP security team released emergency security patches for two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) tracked collectively as PHP2Shell.
The two unauthenticated RCE flaws were discovered by Calif, OpenAI, and Wiz security researchers, and affect all PHP installations that serve web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed.
"We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs," the PHP security team said.
Both flaws stem from the same underlying problem: PHP can leave its memory in a corrupted state when a request ends abnormally, and both can be exploited to achieve remote code execution.
CVE-2026-109618 can be used to gain remote code execution as the web worker account by exploiting a chain of weaknesses that trigger out-of-memory corruption, while the CVE-2026-109619 stale global state vulnerability enables unauthenticated heap use-after-free, memory disclosure, and remote code execution with the web worker's privileges.
Admins should install PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35 as soon as possible on servers running PHP 8.x and migrate to a fixed release if they're running PHP 7 or earlier.

articles.title: AI sped up coding. Sonar instills confidence with verification.
articles.summary:
AI sped up coding. Sonar instills confidence with verification.
AI coding tools can produce a striking burst of productivity — but the initial surge may not last. A Carnegie Mellon study of public repositories adopting Cursor found a three- to five-fold increase in lines added during the first month, with the gains dissipating after roughly two months. The study, which used SonarQube (Sonar’s core platform) to measure code quality, also found that static analysis warnings rose by 30% and code complexity by 41%. The short-term velocity boost therefore comes with a persistent increase in technical debt.
Tom Howlett, Sonar’s Director of AI Engineering Engagement, tells The New Stack that while coding has sped up, verification, which many teams still rely on manual code review to do, hasn’t kept pace. If developers generate 50 times more code while relying on the same review process, time spent on code review rises and becomes a bottleneck, Howlett tells The New Stack.
There’s another complication. Agents don’t always know how to make the smallest change needed to deliver a feature. Without sufficient context about the codebase, they can make assumptions, generate unnecessary code, and add to technical debt. As Howlett puts it, you end up with more complex, verbose code, which makes the problem worse.

Toute cette affaire est l’occasion de faire un bref pas de côté, pour faire un petit point de culture générale en informatique, car PHP est un acronyme qui a historiquement deux significations. Il existe en effet une explication officielle, ainsi qu’un sens historique.
Quand on demande à la foire aux questions du site officiel PHP.net ce que veut dire PHP, la réponse a tout l’air d’une vanne de développeur : « PHP : Hypertext Preprocessor », soit un préprocesseur hypertexte, c’est-à-dire un programme informatique qui fabrique les pages web avant de les envoyer au navigateur, pour les afficher à l’internaute.
Sauf que le premier mot du sigle est le sigle lui-même, ce qui embrouille beaucoup de monde, reconnaît la documentation.
En fait, c’est ce qu’on appelle un acronyme récursif. On retrouve ce même clin d’œil chez GNU, le projet de système d’exploitation libre dont le nom signifie « GNU’s Not Unix ». C’est l’exemple le plus connu, mais on en trouve d’autres, comme l’émulateur WINE, dont le nom signifie… « Wine Is Not an Emulator ».

articles.title: From feral to fiduciary: making AI agents serve your interests
articles.summary:
From feral to fiduciary: making AI agents serve your interests
Tech leaders face a dilemma as they prepare to put AI agents into production. They want the higher productivity and lower costs that AI agents can provide. But they fear unknown risks from AI capabilities that differ from the rest of their software stack. When an agent makes decisions and takes actions on its own, it might be doing its best work. It might also be doing its worst.
As AI agents become more capable, organizations want assurance that their oversight can keep up. How do they strike the right balance between innovation and risk? It comes down to how well they can assess, measure, and maintain trust in their agents. The more trust agents earn, the more autonomy they can be granted.
Trust as a line of credit
Think about the way credit card risk is managed. When you apply for a card, the issuer assesses your credit history and ability to repay before setting a credit limit. Then, once you have your card, payments are subject to real-time authorization and fraud controls. Unusual transactions can trigger additional scrutiny. Paying your card on time may improve your credit score, but it won’t automatically increase your credit limit.
AI agents should be treated similarly.

articles.title: PVTW: Extending Silicon Characterization From PVT To Real-World Workload
articles.summary:
Two devices operating at exactly the same voltage, frequency, and temperature can behave differently depending on what they are being asked to do.
For decades, silicon characterization has been built around Process, Voltage, and Temperature, or PVT. We characterize devices across process variation, sweep voltage and frequency, control temperature, generate SHMOO plots, and establish the operating envelope of the silicon.
That methodology remains fundamental. But today’s high-performance processors are increasingly systems in their own right. An AI accelerator may contain thousands of compute elements, distributed SRAM, high-speed SerDes, PCIe and Ethernet interfaces, multiple clock and power domains, advanced packaging, firmware, operating systems, compilers and application software.
This suggests adding another dimension: PVTW: Process × Voltage × Temperature × Workload
Frequency can be swept within this characterization space to determine operating margin.
The objective is not to replace traditional ATE characterization with System Level Test. It is to combine the electrical precision and control available from ATE with the realistic operating environment available from SLT, while retaining the ability to use either independently.
One way to implement PVTW is through a hybrid characterization architecture integrating ATE resources and SLT capability.

Recursive, an AI startup founded last year, is starting to live up to its name. The company, which is trying to build AI that can improve itself, released its first model, Flint, on Wednesday. Flint is a free coding model that can run on a laptop and was built largely with the help of AI.
Recursive’s automated research system, which it calls the Eureka Machine, helped with nearly every step of Flint’s development, the company says. That let a small team build the model from scratch in under four months.
Flint is an early public test of recursive self-improvement: the idea that AI can build better AI, which in turn builds even better AI. It’s also one of the most debated ideas in the industry. Some researchers fear that AI improving itself could slip out of human control. For now, Recursive’s version is more limited: an AI research assistant overseen by people that produced a model small enough for a laptop.
The company emerged from stealth in May with $650 million in funding at a $4.65 billion valuation, from backers including GV, Nvidia, and AMD Ventures. Recursive is led by CEO Richard Socher, Salesforce’s former chief scientist.
Because Flint runs on a user’s own computer rather than a company’s cloud servers, developers can use it offline, keep their code private, and avoid the usage fees that AI cloud services charge based on how much text the model processes. articles.title: Article Series: Agentic AI Architecture
articles.summary:
The IT industry is changing before our very eyes. With AI entering the software architecture and development landscape, whether we like it or not, we are set to be taken on a roller coaster, the likes of which we haven’t seen since the advent of microservices and cloud-native computing. If the last decade was spent mostly on mastering and optimizing the cloud and micro- or nano-scale service-oriented architecture, the next decade will likely be spent figuring out how to master AI for building a new generation of IT systems.
These new systems will harness the power of AI in ways that, even today, are perhaps not fully comprehensible, as this space is moving forward at a neck-breaking pace, and last year’s best practice is this year’s antipattern. This rapid pace of innovation comes with many challenges, but can also be exciting for those willing to join the ride.
In this series, we try to establish agentic AI architecture as a new type of software architecture that will likely dominate the industry for years to come. The articles, written by industry experts, cover various elements and aspects of agentic AI architecture. We aim to present the latest trends and developments shaping the new type of architecture as it enters the mainstream.

articles.summary:

He added that paying a "dividend" would help make the sites popular, though similar incentives haven't always worked in the past.
"I have watched the process closely, and data centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck," Trump said in a Truth Social post.
The president added that these dividends should be paid to the community and/or individuals within the community.
While everyone likes free money, not everyone believes a cash incentive is worth having a data center at their front door. It was reported in September that every household in Hazle Township, Pennsylvania, was promised a $10,000 "grant" from a data center developer. The money is contingent on approval of the first of up to 15 data center buildings on a 1,300-acre site at the foot of the Pocono Mountains near the town.

articles.title: Signal Vulnerability Lets Malicious Callers Block Hang-Ups
articles.summary:
Signal has resolved a critical-severity vulnerability that could allow a malicious caller to keep audio and video tracks enabled even after the user hung up.
The security defect is tracked as CVE-2026-113380 (CVSS score of 9.3) and impacts RingRTC, the open source library Signal uses for voice and video calls, which is based on WebRTC.
Due to the issue, a remote peer could flood the call’s Finite State Machine (FSM) event queue with junk, and the call would not terminate.
This happened because the hangup was not treated as a kill switch, but as an event added to the FSM event queue; there was no rate limit on peer-originated events; and the hangup event had no priority.
“Flood the queue with junk and the hang-up waits behind attacker noise forever, so the call (microphone, possibly camera) is never torn down,” a GitHub write-up by a researcher reads.
By exploiting the vulnerability, an attacker could keep the audio and video tracks flowing from a target device while the victim believes they ended the call.
The security defect was resolved in RingRTC version 2.72.0, which was released on September 4.
Details on the flaw, however, were published on Tuesday, along with a conceptual proof-of-concept (PoC). NIST added the CVE to the NVD database on Tuesday.
Signal resolved the issue by ensuring that call termination requests do not remain blocked in FSM’s event queue and are detected independently.

articles.title: Why Yango doesn't see Africa's fragmentation as a flaw
articles.summary:
Ask any founder who has built a business across different African markets, and they would agree the continent’s digital market is fragmented. The fragmentation shows up in how people pay, how businesses are regulated, consumer behaviour, and how digital services are delivered.
Companies also face different licencing requirements, tax regimes, data rules, infrastructure availability, and consumer behaviours as they move from one country to the next. Even within a single country, the rules can sometimes change from one city to another.
Norebase’s State of Expansion in Africa 2026 report offers a glimpse into just how different those markets can be. Based on data from more than 40,000 companies that have expanded through its platform, the report found differences in how long it takes to establish a business across African countries, as well as the rules and requirements companies have to navigate.
Yango Group, a Dubai-headquartered company that provides digital services, including mobility, delivery, foodtech, and entertainment across over 30 countries, has had to contend with many of those differences as it expands across African markets.
However, Adeniyi Adebayo, the company’s Chief Business Officer, sees the fragmentation differently. In an interview with TechCabal in October, he argued that while Africa is undoubtedly fragmented, the differences are more nuanced than they are often made out to be.

articles.title: CISA: Hackers chain Plex flaws in Plex2Shell attacks to breach servers
articles.summary:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) is warning that attackers are actively exploiting four vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server.
The security issues are collectively called Plex2Shell. When chained in an exploit, an attacker can obtain the owner's admin token and execute code with elevated privileges.
Plex Media Server is a popular media suite that helps users organize personal collections of movies, TV shows, music, and photos, and stream them to other devices at home or remotely over the internet.
CISA has directed federal agencies to prioritize patching systems affected by Plex2Shell vulnerabilities or apply mitigations by October 23.
The security issues were discovered by security researcher Zach Main, who reported them responsibly to Plex on July 27.
The individual flaws are rated medium to high in severity, but the researcher assigns the full exploit chain a critical score of 9.8.
- CVE-2026-96652 – An SSRF flaw in /player/timeline that allows unauthenticated attackers to make Plex send POST requests to arbitrary destinations, including its own internal APIs.
- CVE-2026-96654 – A URL injection flaw in searchOne that allows attackers to invoke other plugins’ functions with attacker-controlled parameters.
- CVE-2026-96655 – An authenticated SSRF flaw in the transcoder endpoint that allows users to make Plex request arbitrary internal or external addresses.
