articles.summary:
Amodei says Anthropic’s safety delay may have cost it an AI lead
Anthropic first released Mythos-class models in February 2026, but CEO Dario Amodei said it delayed broader access until June to build stronger cybersecurity safeguards.
Amodei laid out that reasoning Tuesday in a lengthy post on X, written in response to criticism from Nathan Calvin and defending the company’s approach to AI safety. He conceded the decision may have cost Anthropic a competitive edge. Releasing the models sooner, he argues, would have given organizations less time to prepare their infrastructure for increasingly capable AI-powered cyberattacks.
“We likely sacrificed a significant chunk of a several-month model lead,” Amodei writes.
Anthropic tells The New Stack that the delay follows a commitment in its Responsible Scaling Policy to require a strong argument that catastrophic risk is contained and to delay development and deployment as far as needed until it no longer believes it holds a significant lead.
Sparring over a strategy under scrutiny
In his criticism posted Monday, Calvin argues that Anthropic increasingly resembles a company racing to build superintelligence while weakening its commitments to preventing dangerous AI outcomes.
He points to the company’s more than $500 billion in computing deals, its growing use of AI to develop new models, and changes to its Responsible Scaling Policy, which establishes safeguards as models become more powerful.

Cette baisse de performance a un impact sur l’utilisation des drones ukrainiens et sur les capacités du pays à faire face aux attaques russes. Volodymyr Zelensky avait déclaré à ce propos : « Starlink n’a pas été désactivé, sa vitesse a simplement été réduite. Personne ne se dit responsable
Le 14 octobre dernier, en réponse à un post X du ministre de la Défense ukrainienne faisant état des performances de Starshield, Elon Musk semble s’être dédouané de toute responsabilité : « Les systèmes Starshield sont détenus et contrôlés par le gouvernement américain. articles.title: SA’s Happy Pay launches pay-per-sale ad platform after $6.1m pilot - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
South African buy now, pay later (BNPL) platform Happy Pay has publicly launched Happy Ads, an AI-powered performance media platform that only charges retailers when a campaign results in a sale.
Happy Pay provides zero-cost installment payments through its ad-subsidised payments network. Its platform connects merchants with high-intent shoppers, enabling consumers to split purchases into interest-free installments while helping retailers grow through performance-based customer acquisition, conversion, and basket expansion. The company raised a US$5 million seed round back in March.
Happy Ads lets brands promote products and offers to Happy Pay’s more than 800,000 registered users, as well as two million customers across its partner network. It generated more than ZAR100 million (US$6.1 million) in merchant sales during its pilot phase, delivering more than 268 million impressions and an average 20x return on ad spend. Happy Pay says a further six million users are set to join the network soon.
Unlike traditional digital advertising, where brands pay for impressions or clicks, Happy Ads works on a cost-per-acquisition model. Retailers set the commission they are willing to pay and are only charged when a campaign converts into a completed sale.

articles.title: Why you don't need an audiophile headset for gaming — comfort, convenience, and a good mic win over pure audio fidelity
articles.summary:
Why you don't need an audiophile headset for gaming — comfort, convenience, and a good mic win over pure audio fidelity
Audiophile headsets are all about audio fidelity — but that's not really what most gamers are looking for.
"Best gaming headset for audiophiles" is one of the categories on our list of best gaming headsets, and it's easy to look at that and wonder if you shouldn't be looking at just audiophile headsets to begin with. Headsets are mainly about audio, after all, and it does seem to logically follow that audiophile headsets would have the best audio (I mean, it's in the name).
Well, not so fast.
Headsets are mainly about audio, but that doesn't mean that the "objectively" best-sounding headset by audiophile standards translates to the best-sounding headset by gaming standards. Nor does it mean that you should choose your gaming headset based on audio quality at the expense of everything else.
Audiophile headsets, including headphones, are primarily designed around one thing: audio fidelity. In other words, they're designed and tuned to reproduce audio exactly as it was recorded, which is exactly as the artist heard it when they were recording it, and is therefore exactly as the artist intended for it to be heard. This doesn't necessarily mean it's going to sound amazing to everyone. articles.title: Netflix Bridges AWS IAM and Internal Identity with Workload Attestation
articles.summary:
Netflix has developed a workload attestation mechanism that allows Apache Spark jobs running on Amazon EMR to exchange their AWS execution identity for a short-lived internal workload identity. The approach bridges AWS IAM with Netflix’s internal Metatron PKI, allowing managed compute workloads to authenticate to internal services without manually injecting credentials.
Dhruv Pratap, Big Data Platform Engineer at Netflix, described the design in a LinkedIn post as
On infrastructure you build yourself, you can bootstrap your own identity however you like.
Netflix operates two identity systems. AWS provides managed workloads with an IAM execution role, while internal services use Metatron, a private PKI that issues short-lived X.509 certificates for mutual TLS. Netflix also uses Data Projects as the ownership and identity boundary for data access. A Spark job running on EMR therefore needs to establish that its AWS identity corresponds to the internal identity associated with its Data Project.
The design maps each Data Project to a dedicated IAM role. Because Netflix expects Data Projects to reach the tens of thousands, these roles are deterministically distributed across a pool of dedicated AWS accounts rather than concentrated in one account.

articles.title: Lazarus hackers use post-quantum cryptography for malware delivery
articles.summary:
North Korean hackers are using a post-quantum cryptographic mechanism to secure malicious payload delivery in new operations that combine old and new malware.
The campaign targets South Korean organizations through a “rather complex” infection chain. Researchers at cybersecurity company Kaspersky dubbed the operation FlashHole and attributed it to the Lazarus Group.
Analysis of the malware revealed that the threat actor used the standardized ML-KEM post-quantum cryptographic mechanism to communicate with the command-and-control (C2) server for malware delivery.
Kaspersky says the attackers used LPEClient malware, previously associated with Lazarus, to receive ML-KEM-1024 public keys from its C2 infrastructure and generate shared keys that allowed it to decrypt subsequently incoming payloads.
According to the researchers, the attacks started in July 2025 and relied on phishing pages directing targets to specially crafted GitHub pages.
These pages load JavaScript code from external domains, triggering an in-memory execution chain that involved INISAFE CrossWeb EX, a security tool popular in South Korea.
The security tool’s process executed the legitimate Windows binary fsquirt.exe, which was used to run shellcode that installed TechHub, a downloader responsible for retrieving additional malware from private GitHub repositories.

articles.title: AI found flaws in the code behind 70% of the web. The fix took two months.
articles.summary:
AI found flaws in the code behind 70% of the web. The fix took two months.
PHP powers roughly 70% of the world’s websites, according to Wiz Research, so a flaw in its core engine affects much more than any single application. On Wednesday, researchers disclosed two critical vulnerabilities discovered with help from frontier AI models. OpenAI also proposed a new framework for handling the growing number of security flaws AI is helping uncover.
The flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and collectively called PHP2Shell, score 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 severity scale. Researchers at Calif.io found one using OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol, while Wiz independently found both using its Wiz Atlas tool alongside Google’s Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol. Cloudflare also lists Quarkslab among the parties that disclosed the bugs.
A Decade of Dormant Defects
The problem starts with how PHP handles errors. When a request runs out of memory or crashes, PHP can leave behind references to memory that has already been freed. The next request handled by the same worker process may still treat those references as valid. Wiz found that attackers could exploit this behavior to access sensitive data or run malicious code.
These are memory-safety bugs, including use-after-free and type confusion, that developers have spent years trying to prevent by moving critical C code to languages like Rust. PHP’s engine is written in C, and Wiz showed that attackers could exploit the flaws to run code on WordP…

articles.title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
articles.summary:
Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate Certificate Authority (CA) certificates have been compromised, making it trivial for attackers to forge certificates that would be trusted by unpatched roots of trust. Six of the impacted certificates were for Transport Layer Security (TLS) and trusted by the Apple, Chrome, Microsoft and Mozilla root programs. The other two certificates were for codesigning and trusted by Microsoft. Browsers were able to block the affected intermediate CAs using their background revocation blocklists, but most other software relying on web public key infrastructure (PKI) lacks any mechanism to filter intermediate CAs. In order to defend against rogue certificates from the compromised intermediate CAs many projects have chosen to remove the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from their roots of trust. That removal is causing collateral damage for all legitimate certificates previously issued by CAs chained to that root.
Forged certificates can potentially be used to impersonate sites and services as part of a man in the middle (MITM) attack. The underlying problem is that there are hundreds of CAs in a typical root CA bundle, and thousands of intermediate CAs that inherit trust. Any one of those CAs can create a legitimate looking certificate for any domain. The chain of trust is only broken if the trust anchors are updated to reflect the compromise. This leaves any unpatched system vulnerable.

It’s also a standalone prequel to RGG’s Like a Dragon series, chronicling Makoto’s formation of the yakuza organization Tojo Clan that features prominently in those other games.

Le Reich était-il à deux doigts du réacteur atomique ? Werner Heisenberg l’a juré en 1947. Nourri par deux cubes d’uranium rescapés, un jumeau numérique de sa dernière pile a recalculé sa copie en 1 222 simulations : il manquait la moitié de l’uranium et plus de la moitié de l’eau lourde. Plus que tout ce que l’Allemagne possédait.
Avril 1945, Haigerloch, dans le sud-ouest de l’Allemagne. Au fond d’une cave creusée dans la roche, l’équipe de Werner Heisenberg plonge 664 cubes d’uranium naturel, suspendus à des chaînes, dans une cuve d’eau lourde. Baptisée B8, cette pile devait amorcer une réaction en chaîne auto-entretenue, première marche vers le plutonium. Elle n’a jamais démarré. Quatre mois plus tard, les Américains larguaient leur bombe sur Hiroshima.
	
Une quantité relativement faible d'uranium aurait, selon toute probabilité, suffi.
Publiée dans Nature en 1947, cette version du Nobel de physique 1932 a longtemps fait foi. Une étude parue le 29 septembre dans PNAS Nexus, menée par Patrick Park, doctorant à Princeton, et Timothy Koeth, de l'université du Maryland, la démonte chiffres à l'appui.

articles.title: RIP BioWare: EA shuts down storied RPG studio after over three decades

The legendary studio behind series like Mass Effect, Dragon Age, Neverwinter Nights, and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic is no more. BioWare announced via social media Wednesday afternoon that “after more than three decades of shared adventures, BioWare is closing and early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending.”
The official announcement was posted mere minutes after a Bloomberg report detailed 400 job cuts across BioWare parent company Electronic Arts, including 50 at BioWare, based on reports from “a person familiar with the company’s plans.”
“Across our portfolio, we’re making deliberate choices to align talent and investments where we see the greatest opportunities for players and long-term growth,” EA executives wrote in a message to staff, according to Bloomberg.
A long time coming
Following its 1995 founding in Edmonton, Alberta, BioWare first came under the EA umbrella through a 2007 purchase, before Mass Effect and Dragon Age were even a thing. At the time, EA’s then-CEO, John Riccitiello, called BioWare one of “the most respected studios in the industry” that would “make a strong contribution to our strategic growth initiatives on quality, online gaming and developing new intellectual properties. articles.title: Arnaques en ligne : malgré la nouvelle loi, votre banque peut encore refuser de vous rembourser
articles.summary:
Le 15 octobre 2026, la Cour de justice de l’Union européenne (CJUE) a fini par trancher sur la question des remboursements accordés aux victimes d’arnaques en ligne. La plus haute juridiction de l’Union européenne a statué qu’une banque doit rembourser un paiement « non autorisé », même si le client a commis une « négligence grave ».
La banque peut complètement s’abstenir de rembourser son client dans un seul cas bien particulier. Si la banque soupçonne une fraude du client lui-même, elle peut refuser le remboursement. Si elle a « des motifs raisonnables de soupçonner une fraude de la part du client lui-même », la banque n’a fort logiquement pas l’obligation de rembourser l’utilisateur. Par ailleurs, la banque peut récupérer la somme remboursée ultérieurement si elle prouve que le client a commis une négligence grave, mettant en danger ses avoirs. En clair, la banque doit d’abord verser de l’argent à son client, avant de tenter de prouver qu’une négligence a eu lieu.
Sur le papier, ce changement est une excellente nouvelle pour les clients et les victimes. Ceux-ci ne risquent plus de se retrouver sans le sou à la suite d’une escroquerie. En pratique, les banques ne sont pas prêtes à changer leur fusil d’épaule, et vont tout faire pour éviter d’avoir à vous rembourser.

articles.title: Harbor Adds Docker Sandboxes to Run Reproducible AI Agent Evals in Isolated MicroVMs
articles.summary:
Docker announced that Harbor, the open-source agent evaluation framework, now works with Docker Sandboxes. This change allows each evaluation task to run in its own microVM. So, instead of sharing a container, tasks are isolated for better performance. The same tasks run locally or in Docker Cloud Sandboxes, and Docker says it has tested Harbor with 64 concurrent tasks in the cloud.
Evaluating a coding agent means letting it install packages, edit files, and run commands, and a benchmark repeats this thousands of times. Docker's engineers describe this as running untrusted, AI-written code at scale. They also flag reward hacking, where an agent earns a passing score by tampering with tests or overwriting the file that records its score instead of solving the task. Harbor manages orchestration. It runs tasks, collects scores, and logs. It also supports benchmarks like Terminal-Bench. It needs an execution environment that is both isolated and consistent.
Each task runs in a Docker Sandbox, a microVM with its own kernel, so agent activity stays inside the VM and cannot reach the host, other tasks, or anything outside the environment. In Docker Cloud Sandboxes, configurable network policies let a task pull dependencies during setup, then restrict internet access while the agent works. Pendant l’exercice interarmées Typhon, organisé du 5 au 16 octobre, l’armée a entraîné ses forces à défendre le port militaire de Toulon, avec des manœuvres aériennes où des drones étaient engagés. D’autres drones, non autorisés ceux-là, ont survolé de nuit la base navale, un site de la Direction générale de l’armement (DGA) et le 54e régiment d’artillerie d’Hyères entre le 9 et le 13 octobre, selon ICI Provence. « Ils étaient en tout cas plusieurs à chaque fois, et des gros engins », a confié une source à nos confrères. La préfecture maritime a confirmé ces survols, et le parquet de Toulon a ouvert une enquête judiciaire. articles.title: Meta suspends Muse sharing after sensitive documents turn up in shared chats

What we know so far: Meta has paused the conversation-sharing feature in its Muse AI assistant after security researchers discovered thousands of links in public DNS records. Some of the links exposed sensitive business documents and personal financial information that anyone could access without logging in. Researchers at security firm Claroc traced the exposure to the way Muse generated its web addresses.
Each shared conversation had a hostname containing a descriptive title and a random identifier. Both could appear in searchable DNS records, giving researchers the information they needed to reconstruct the link and open the page.
"People have the ability to share specific Muse artifacts, which creates a page that can be accessed by those with the link," Muse spokesperson Tracy Clayton said in a statement to The Verge. "However, we've paused this functionality while we review this report and consider changes to how these links can be discovered."
Sharing tools commonly rely on long, random strings in their URLs to prevent outsiders from guessing an address. Muse used random identifiers that Claroc said were long enough to resist guessing. The weakness lay in where Muse placed them: in the hostname, alongside a title describing the conversation.

articles.title: AI Changes the Data Interface, Not the Query Engine
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- An AI agent that reads Parquet still depends on an execution engine; AI changes the analytical interface and interpretation layer, not the need for precise computation.
- Separate deterministic computation from probabilistic reasoning. Engines should filter, aggregate, and join, while agents should interpret evidence and communicate conclusions.
- An embedded engine such as DuckDB can be sufficient when the data volume is moderate, the primary consumer is the agent workflow, and writes are controlled.
- A managed lakehouse becomes valuable when data has multiple independent consumers, must join with large shared datasets, requires concurrent writes, or needs organization-wide governance.
- Production-grade agent analytics should retain the source data, configuration, derived facts, and model outputs so that every report can be validated and replayed.
AI agents can now generate analytical code, read files from object storage, and turn operational data into structured reports. Does that make data lakes, lakehouses, and SQL engines obsolete? We encountered this question while automating the analysis of a large disaster-recovery exercise. Our first working design stored thirty-second service metrics as Parquet in S3-compatible object storage, used DuckDB for deterministic aggregation, and asked an AI agent to classify failover outcomes and explain the evidence. articles.title: Tesla profits drop 43% in Q3
articles.summary:
Tesla published its third-quarter 2026 financial results this afternoon. Earlier in October, it reported its sales and deliveries for the three-month period, selling fewer cars than in the same quarter in 2025, yet it still beat analyst projections. Now we can see how those sales translate to the bottom line. Tesla brought in $28 billion in revenue in Q3, almost the same as in 2025.
Automotive revenues were $20.6 billion, a 3 percent decrease year over year. Perhaps more troubling is the decline in revenue from solar panels and storage batteries—this line of business had been growing, but for Q3 revenue fell 16 percent year over year to $2.9 billion. Services and other revenues, though, which include parts and Supercharger use, grew by a third to $4.6 billion.
But the company—like the rest of us—has seen its expenses go up. Operating expenses rose by 39 percent to $4.8 billion, dropping the company’s operating margin to just 2.6 percent; in Q3 2025, Tesla’s margin was 5.8 percent. Net profit fell to $787 million, down 43 percent year over year. What’s more, capital expenditures were up by 110 percent to $4.7 billion, and free cash flow was down 62 percent to $1.5 billion.

Su diseño y mecánica de uso no solo sostienen un mercado activo de reediciones, sino que sirven como modelo estructural para los nuevos agentes de IA impulsados por compañías tecnológicas de alcance global.
Orígenes y mecánica del Tamagotchi
Creado por la empresa japonesa Bandai y comercializado a partir de 1996, el Tamagotchi es un dispositivo de bolsillo con forma de huevo, equipado con un procesador básico, una pantalla LCD monocromática y tres botones físicos. Su software simula el ciclo de vida ininterrumpido de una criatura alienígena virtual.
La mecánica de uso exige la interacción activa y constante del propietario. A través de la interfaz de tres botones, el usuario debe gestionar indicadores de hambre, felicidad y disciplina, lo que implica alimentar a la mascota, jugar minijuegos, limpiar su entorno y administrar medicinas cuando enferma.
El algoritmo interno evalúa la constancia y calidad de estos cuidados para determinar en qué tipo de criatura adulta evolucionará el personaje. Si se ignoran las alertas del dispositivo, la mascota virtual fallece, obligando al usuario a reiniciar el equipo y comenzar el ciclo desde la fase de incubación.

Vercel Labs has released fx as open source, an experimental coding agent and command-line tool written in Zig and built to be scripted or embedded rather than run as a full-screen terminal application.
Announced in August 2026, fx ships as a 6.3 MiB native binary with a reported single-digit-megabyte memory baseline and a 10-microsecond cold start, figures Vercel states rather than independently verified benchmarks. Instead of taking over the terminal with a persistent interface, fx writes its conversation into ordinary scrollback and exposes the same engine through both a CLI and a library.
The result is aimed at developers building agent infrastructure more than at people looking for another chat window. Structured output is available for automation, so a script or CI job can call a command and parse the response:

Editors can attach over the Agent Client Protocol using fx acp, and libfx exposes the engine to JavaScript, including a WebAssembly build.

Quatre clés post-quantiques pour cacher le logiciel espion
Lazarus inventorie les machines infectées avec LPEClient depuis 2019 et ses développeurs ont profondément remanié ce programme. articles.title: Lo que ha sucedido con PHP nos avisa: tenemos un problema grave con el software antiguo que sostiene internet
articles.summary:
La infraestructura que sostiene internet está envejeciendo. Es natural que sea así, pero lo que hace apenas tres años no habríamos podido anticipar es que la llegada de los modelos de inteligencia artificial (IA) de frontera iba a acelerar drásticamente su envejecimiento. Tenemos un problema. Lo que ha sucedido con el lenguaje de programación PHP demuestra que la seguridad de internet nos exige mantener y revisar tecnologías que llevan décadas en funcionamiento, y que hoy pueden ser más vulnerables que nunca.
La IA nos está ayudando a encontrar vulnerabilidades que habían pasado inadvertidas durante años, pero identificarlas no es suficiente; también es imprescindible corregirlas, y hacerlo en una infraestructura tan grande y heterogénea como es internet no es fácil. Lo que acaba de pasar con PHP puede ayudarnos a entender con precisión a qué nos enfrentamos. Este lenguaje fue concebido para desarrollar aplicaciones web, y es importante porque tiene un rol central en el ecosistema de aplicaciones y servicios que lo utilizan como parte de su infraestructura.
Que un sistema funcione correctamente durante muchos años no nos garantiza que no tenga defectos y que sea seguro. Los programadores que escriben su código a menudo se ven obligados a preservar la compatibilidad con las aplicaciones, las bibliotecas, y también con aquellas extensiones que dependen de su comportamiento. CVE-2026-110264 stems from an integer overflow weakness in GitLab's Regular Expression Compiler, a background engine that parses and validates regular expressions in configuration files.

"GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server due to integer overflow when compiling a specially crafted regular expression," the company said.
"We strongly recommend that all installations running a version affected by the issues described below are upgraded to the latest version as soon as possible. articles.title: Investigan a Booking.com en la Comisión Europea por protección a los viajeros de anuncios fraudulentos y estafas
articles.summary:
Booking.com es investigada por la Comisión Europea por una posible infracción de la Ley de Servicios Digitales (DSA). El órgano ejecutivo europeo analiza si la plataforma evaluó y redujo de forma adecuada los riesgos de anuncios fraudulentos y estafas por suplantación de identidad.
La investigación busca determinar si la empresa protege a los usuarios frente a alojamientos inexistentes, ofertas engañosas y mensajes destinados a obtener datos personales o solicitar pagos fraudulentos.
La Comisión también revisa si Booking.com identifica con claridad los anuncios pagados. Los proveedores de alojamiento pueden pagar una comisión más alta para aparecer en posiciones destacadas de los resultados de búsqueda, pero los usuarios deben poder reconocer que se trata de publicidad.
Qué investiga la Comisión Europea sobre Booking
La Comisión Europea examinará cómo Booking.com detecta y elimina anuncios fraudulentos, incluidos los vinculados con alojamientos inexistentes, suplantación de identidad y ofertas que incumplen la normativa.
El órgano ejecutivo de Europa también revisará el sistema de mensajería de la plataforma y la forma en que se comparten los datos de reservas y huéspedes con los proveedores de alojamiento. El objetivo es comprobar si existen garantías suficientes para impedir que esa información se use en estafas de phishing o para solicitar pagos fraudulentos.

articles.title: Comme WhatsApp, ChatGPT met enfin vos conversations sous clé
articles.summary:
OpenAI déploie depuis le 20 octobre les « conversations verrouillées » dans ChatGPT, du compte gratuit aux offres Enterprise et Edu. Le dispositif rappelle le verrouillage des discussions que WhatsApp propose depuis le 15 mai 2023 : un code à quatre chiffres, ou Face ID et Touch ID sur mobile, et le fil disparaît des écrans. La fonction, repérée dès le mois d’août dans le code de l’application Android, arrive progressivement sur le web, les téléphones et les applications de bureau.
Un dossier sous code, invisible dans l’historique
Une fois verrouillée, la conversation rejoint un espace dédié et s’efface de l’historique, des fils épinglés et des résultats de recherche. L’ouvrir réclame le code, ou la biométrie du téléphone, et un geste suffit ensuite pour rendre le fil à la circulation générale. Le dossier « Conversations verrouillées » reste visible dans l’interface. WhatsApp propose depuis fin 2023 un code secret qui masque jusqu’à l’existence du dossier, un cran de discrétion encore hors de portée de ChatGPT. Le déploiement s’étalant sur plusieurs semaines, l’option peut d’ailleurs encore manquer à l’appel sur certains comptes.
Les conversations temporaires, les archives, les discussions de groupe ou celles liées à une tâche programmée restent hors du périmètre. Sur ordinateur, il faut passer par la dernière mise à jour des applications macOS et Windows, avec un déploiement graduel toujours en cours selon OpenAI. La mémoire suit le même cloisonnement. articles.title: 9 Minuten Laden, 90 Minuten Arbeit: Neue Akkus sollen den Digits 5 zum echten Haushaltshelfer machen
articles.summary:
9 Minuten laden für 90 Minuten Arbeit: Wie neue Akkus humanoide Roboter alltagstauglich machen
Der humanoide Roboter Digit 5 von Agility Robotics hat eine besonders lange Laufzeit bei kurzem Aufladen. Die Batterietechnik dafür liefert das Unternehmen Nyobolt. Damit kommt der Roboter auf ein Verhältnis von Laufzeit zu Ladezeit von ungefähr 10:1. Für jede Minute an der Ladestation stehen also zehn Minuten Arbeit zur Verfügung. Lädt man neun Minuten, läuft der Humanoid 90 Minuten. Der Vorgänger Digit 4 schaffte lediglich ein Verhältnis von 2:1 – er verbrachte rund ein Drittel des Tages am Ladegerät.
Warum Akkus bei Humanoiden das Hauptproblem sind
Humanoide Roboter brauchen viel Strom. Weil sie sich frei bewegen sollen, kommt der aus Batterien. Die halten allerdings nicht lange und müssen regelmäßig nachgeladen oder getauscht werden. Agility Robotics setzt deshalb auf besonders leichte Akkus mit hoher Leistungsdichte, die also viel Energie pro Kilogramm abgeben können.
Mit der neuen Technik könne Digit 5 täglich mehr als zwei komplette Arbeitsschichten absolvieren, teilt Agility Robotics mit. Die Auslastung einer Roboterflotte im Unternehmen steige dadurch deutlich. Die Akkus von Nyobolt sollen zudem viele Ladezyklen überstehen. Konkrete Zahlen nannten allerdings weder Agility Robotics noch Nyobolt: Weder zur Kapazität noch zur Zahl der möglichen Ladevorgänge gibt es Angaben.
Warum kein Wechselakku?

articles.title: Xbox wants you to pay 24 to 40 cents per hour to stream games you already bought
articles.summary:
In September, when Microsoft severely limited the game-streaming buffet available to Game Pass subscribers, the company said non-subscribers would soon be able to “purchase cloud playtime hours through the Xbox Store and stream eligible games they own on supported devices.” Today, Microsoft rolled out those a la carte Cloud Playtime purchases to Xbox Insiders, with prices that might be a bit galling for players who have already purchased these streamable games.
The “introductory launch pricing” for Xbox’s Cloud Playtime purchases is as follows:
- 10 hours for $4 (~$0.40/hour)
- 25 hours for $8 (~$0.32/hour)
- 50 hours for $12 (~$0.24/hour)
Purchased playtime “remains available until it’s used,” Microsoft writes, so you don’t have to worry about your 50-hour purchase expiring before you can use it fully.
Paying for playtime directly like this evokes images of old arcades, where players would invest a quarter or two (in 20th century dollars) often for just a few minutes of gameplay. That kind of metered play has fallen heavily out of fashion, though, in favor of one-time purchases for an all-you-can-play experience at home.
On the surface, paying as low as 24 cents for an hour of streaming game time doesn’t sound completely unreasonable. Remember, though, that these streaming costs come on top of whatever you paid to buy the game in the first place. articles.title: AMD brings official Ryzen overclocking to Linux with AOD driver support — no official app, but third-party options should arrive soon
articles.summary:
AMD brings official Ryzen overclocking to Linux with AOD driver support — no official app, but third-party options should arrive soon
This is a major milestone for improving the DIY tuning experience on Linux.
While Windows overclockers have spent years lazily sliding UI controls to adjust frequency curves and tweak voltages inside Ryzen Master, Linux users have largely had to treat their CPU tuning like an archaeological dig into the opaque veil of UEFI/BIOS firmware. Well, rejoice, Linux users, as AMD has officially published a fresh set of patches for the Linux kernel introducing AOD (AMD Overclocking Driver) support for Ryzen processors, Phoronix reports.
Instead of forcing developers to reverse-engineer closed-source firmware hooks or rely on messy, machine-specific ACPI workarounds, this new kernel driver is a direct pipeline to AMD's platform adjustments. By exposing core tuning capabilities straight through the standard sysfs interface, AMD is laying down an official, upstreamed foundation for software-level CPU management.
Right out of the gate, the driver handles platform-level SMT toggling, memory clock visibility, and power tunables. That's right: you can now toggle Simultaneous Multithreading (SMT) dynamically through this driver interface. That works through the CPU hotplugging mechanism and acts as a clean alternative to passing the old 'nosmt' boot parameter to the kernel. Windows 11 optimiert RAM-Verbrauch: So gut läuft das System jetzt auf einem PC mit 8 Gigabyte
Seit August 2026 arbeitet Microsoft daran, Windows 11 effizienter zu gestalten. Damals hatte das Unternehmen versprochen, dass gerade Geräte mit acht Gigabyte RAM davon stark profitieren sollen. Wie genau diese Speicheroptimierung aussehen sollte, verriet das Unternehmen damals noch nicht. Jetzt zeigen sich aber schon die ersten Auswirkungen. Seit dem Update auf Windows 11 26H2 verbrauchen die besagten Systeme deutlich weniger RAM.

articles.title: Two web emergencies in one week: guessable certificate keys and critical PHP bugs that leaked before patches
articles.summary:
A hot potato: Security teams are dealing with two separate emergencies this week, and both go straight to the foundations of the web. The first is a certificate authority that shipped private keys anyone could guess. The second is a pair of critical PHP flaws that leaked before patches existed. Browsers fixed the certificate problem within hours. Everything else, from Linux servers to Docker images and IoT gear, needs someone to log in and patch.
Eight intermediate certificates issued by India-based certificate authority eMudhra were found to have private keys so weak they can be calculated from the certificates themselves. Those certificates chained to roots trusted by Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Windows, as well as by operating systems and countless software trust stores. Anyone holding one of the keys could issue a valid certificate for any domain and use it to impersonate that site, intercepting or modifying its traffic.
A properly generated P-384 key carries roughly 384 bits of entropy. eMudhra's keys had between 3 and 8 bits, and one of them was simply the number 4. Recovering all eight requires testing no more than 256 values. eMudhra blamed a script error during key generation, which were then used by mistake. That means the keys were exposed for roughly 18 months before a researcher reported the problem this month. The company says most of the certificates never went into production and it has found no evidence of misuse.

articles.title: Can AI make debt collections less about chasing and more about predicting?
articles.summary:
Can AI make debt collections less about chasing and more about predicting?
The future lies in using data to understand portfolios, AI to prioritise decisions, and human judgement where individual circumstances matter most.
Defaults are inevitable.
For the past few years, we have been hearing about predictive analytics that can identify a borrower who is going to default before the default actually happens.
Time and again, we have seen the limits of this idea.
Defaults aren't a prediction problem that technology will eventually eliminate. Defaults are an uncertainty that lending produces, by design. What lenders need is not machinery that assumes this uncertainty can be removed, but machinery designed to operate effectively under it.
You cannot predict at an individual borrower level who is going to default. You can, at best, predict, over a sufficiently large cohort of borrowers, what the default rate might be.
The behaviour of large groups can be predicted statistically. The behaviour of a particular individual cannot.
If you have one million borrowers, you can make remarkably good statements about what will happen to the portfolio. Narrow it to 100,000 borrowers in Karnataka, and you can still make useful predictions. Narrow it further by repayment history, geography, employment, credit score and other risk characteristics, and you can create increasingly meaningful cohorts.
But as the cohorts get smaller, the certainty of those predictions starts decreasing.

articles.title: When GPS Isn't Enough: Building a Second Layer of Positioning - EE Times
articles.summary:
Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) have become invisible infrastructure. Smartphones, vehicles, logistics systems, emergency services, and critical infrastructure increasingly depend on reliable satellite positioning being available whenever it is needed.
That assumption is increasingly being challenged. GNSS signals are very weak by the time they reach Earth. Jamming can prevent a receiver from obtaining a usable signal, while spoofing can cause it to calculate the wrong location. Satellite visibility can also be limited indoors, inside shipping containers, and among dense urban structures.
The risk is no longer theoretical. In 2025, the European Union Aviation Safety Agency and the International Air Transport Association (IATA) reported increasing GNSS interference across EMEA. IATA data showed a 220% increase in GPS signal-loss events between 2021 and 2024. In April 2024, two Finnair flights could not land at Tartu, Estonia, because interference disrupted the airport’s GPS-dependent approach. Finnair suspended the route until a non-GPS procedure was introduced. Baltic maritime authorities have also reported more frequent interference affecting ships.
Location is now a fundamental input for industrial IoT, logistics, and autonomous machines, where losing position can have operational or safety consequences. The answer is not to replace GNSS. It is to stop treating it as the only positioning layer.

El límite de los transistores tradicionales
Un procesador de computadora contiene miles de millones de transistores, que se encienden y apagan de manera constante para procesar datos y ejecutar instrucciones. Durante décadas, los fabricantes redujeron el tamaño de estos componentes para mejorar el rendimiento y disminuir el consumo de energía.

articles.title: UN says we're going to blow past 1.5º warming, offers a "now what?" answer
articles.summary:
In 2015, all but two countries agreed to make an effort to keep global temperatures from reaching 1.5° C above pre-industrial readings. Since then, most of the world has largely treated what they signed on to as aspirational, and one of the largest emitters (the US) has alternately withdrawn and recommitted to the agreement. Meanwhile, the planet has responded as expected to steadily rising carbon emissions and appears to be practically at the 1.5° limit.
On Wednesday, for the first time, the United Nations Environmental Programme (UNEP) acknowledged that reality, and conceded that the goal of keeping warming below 1.5° was no longer a viable one. Instead, its new goalposts focus on keeping both how long we exceed that limit and how much we exceed it by, at a minimum. Doing that will require both dramatic emissions cuts now and the removal of hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere before the century is out.
Bowing to the inevitable
Depending on which baseline you use to establish pre-industrial temperatures, as well as which reconstruction of global temperatures you rely on, the world has either gotten very close to, or already exceeded the 1.5° milestone. The current El Niño event, which appears exceptionally strong, will almost certainly mean that we’ve gone over it no matter which records you choose.
The UN relies on temperatures averaged over a few decades to determine where we’re at, which means we have technically not gone above the limit yet. But,…

En 1802 apareció en Ourense una piedra con toda una promesa en torno a ella. Una mujer llamada Calpurnia Abana dejó grabado que cumplía con gusto el voto que había hecho a las ninfas de estas aguas, inspirada por un sueño.
Han pasado unos dos mil años y la ciudad sigue haciendo lo mismo que ella: acercarse a unos manantiales que brotan a más de 60 grados en pleno casco histórico. Ahora, eso sí, con bañador y toalla. Porque estas no son como las de Caracalla; estas termas son completamente funcionales. Y no solo los jubilados han cambiado a Benidorm por Salou: este es otro de sus destinos favoritos.
Nació del agua. Según el Concello, los romanos se asentaron en torno a As Burgas y levantaron allí un santuario y unos baños. Las excavaciones han sacado a la luz una piscina del siglo I d. C. y seis piedras votivas dedicadas a Revve Anabaraego, una divinidad indígena de los manantiales. Es decir, el agua ya era sagrada antes de las legiones.
Del muro primitivo se conserva su reforma con hipocausto, el suelo calefactado romano, y las modificaciones medievales. Aquellos suelos calientes explican que los romanos usaran ya chanclas de baño. En la Edad Media, época oscura para el termalismo europeo, los vecinos siguieron usando las fuentes. Hasta el nombre de la ciudad está en disputa: unos lo hacen venir de Aquis Auriensis, el oro del Miño, y otros de aquae urentes, aguas abrasadoras.

articles.title: 333 Tor exit nodes hijacked to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email
articles.summary:
Unknown hackers hijacked more than 300 Tor exit nodes and reconfigured them to favor unencrypted email traffic and redirect SSH connections through servers they controlled, a researcher reported Tuesday.
The hijacking began in late August, when, according to Tor volunteers, the attacker used a valid password that had been reused to gain access to a Tor management server. The attacker then installed Ebury, a backdoor written for Linux that was discovered 12 years ago.
Mysteries remain
Then the attacker connected from the management server to a second Tor server, called Switzerland2, through SSH, using an RSA key that, for unknown reasons, investigators couldn’t find among Switzerland2’s authorized keys. With administrative control of Switzerland2, the attackers installed Ebury there as well. Finally, the attacker reconfigured settings on two exit nodes that Switzerland2 hosted.
Ultimately, 333 exit relays were involved in the SSH and email interception campaign, although investigators haven’t established how the attackers gained control of all the underlying servers. The attackers then reconfigured the servers. One set of changes redirected SSH traffic traversing Tor to one of 12 attacker-controlled interceptor servers. Tor users who ignored warnings that the SSH host key had changed would then enter their SSH passwords.

CBC reports that the data was stolen from Crime Stoppers affiliate P3 Global Intel in March by hacktivist group Internet Yiff Machine, which claimed that it wanted to expose vulnerabilities in the company’s platform. U.S. non-profit Distributed Denial of Secrets ultimately made data available to researchers and journalists, including CBC, to study the impact and warn the public accordingly.

Often, this was street addresses and phone numbers, although CBC reports “tens of thousands” of personal emails and licence plates, as well as “hundreds” of banking details tied to cash rewards, were leaked. There were reportedly even over 4,300 cases of tipsters providing full names, despite Crime Stoppers saying not to do that.

The maintainers of the PHP programming language today released patches for two critical vulnerabilities that affect up to 70% of the world’s websites.

Many municipalities, schools and private companies have taken their advice. Content delivery network operators Cloudflare Inc. and Fastly Inc., meanwhile, reported that hackers are already trying to exploit the bugs.
“This is not a theoretical vulnerability,” said Fastly Chief Product Officer Kelly Shortridge. “We observe many billions of PHP requests a day across Fastly’s global network, and we are seeing evidence of active attacks.”
The two exploits are together known as PHP2Shell. They enable hackers to deploy malicious code on vulnerable servers. The installation process takes only a few seconds in some cases. Once the malware compromises a website, it can read its database and launch cyberattacks against visitors.
The first PHP2Shell exploit emerges when a piece of PHP code receives more data than it can process. PHP responds to such situations by deleting some of the ingested data. According to the language’s maintainers, the data left over after that operation can be used by hackers to launch cyberattacks.

Flapping Airplanes is trying to build AI models that learn from far less data than today’s frontier systems consume. Most of its first year went into new primitives for graphics processing units. That work, according to the company’s announcement on X, enables new algorithms that could “dramatically reshape AI’s cost structure.”
The founders have built what they describe as “the world’s most complete megakernel framework.” Index Ventures Management’s post on the round says a megakernel runs an entire program on a GPU as a single kernel, so the chip stops losing time between steps. Flapping Airplanes says its framework can handle a full training run, serve inference and play a video game at the same time inside one kernel. Memory-bound inference can then overlap with compute-bound training on the same chip.
“A model that’s a million times more data efficient is probably a million times easier to put into the economy,” co-founder Asher Spector told TechCrunch. Spector holds a statistics doctorate from Stanford University.

articles.title: 'It doesn't work': Steve Jobs on why there was never a touchscreen MacBook and why I think he'd totally love what's coming next
articles.summary:
'It doesn't work': Steve Jobs on why there was never a touchscreen MacBook and why I think he'd totally love what's coming next
Ever the contradicitonist
If the rumors are true, next week could mark the introduction of the first-ever touchscreen MacBooks. That's a Mac laptop with a touchscreen. People will probably embrace them and, no, I don't think their arms will fall off.
Steve Jobs famously hated the concept of a touchscreen MacBook. During an October 2010 product launch, he famously dismantled the notion:
"You know, the first thing you think about is this [he gestured toward the image of someone reading out to touch a MacBook screen]. Right, we thought about this years ago. We've done tons of user testing on this, and it turns out it doesn't work. Touch surfaces don't want to be vertical. It gives a great demo, but after a short period of time you start to fatigue, and after an extended period of time your arm wants to fall off; it doesn't work. It's ergonomically terrible. Touch surfaces want to be horizontal, hence touchpads for a notebook. That's why we've perfected our multi-touch trackpads over the years."
In short:
- It doesn't work
- Touch demands horizontal screens
- Your arm gets tired
- Your arm falls off

Pero todo ha cambiado cuando en Francia han anunciado la primera infección registrada por el virus Shamonda en un ser humano y que ha acabado en la muerte.
El primer caso se ha tratado de un paciente que ingresó gravemente enfermo y que finalmente falleció en un hospital de Lyon sin que se haya podido hacer mucho por su vida. Y aunque la ECDC mantiene abierta la investigación para confirmar si el virus fue la causa directa de la muerte o un factor que contribuyó a esta, este hito clínico obliga a cambiar nuestro pensamiento sobre un virus que pensábamos que no nos podía infectar.
El salto a los humanos. Según el comunicado conjunto emitido este mismo jueves por parte de los Ministerios de Agricultura y Sanidad de Francia, la principal hipótesis sobre la transmisión apunta a la picadura de un jején del género Culicoides. Este pequeño insecto hematófago fue muy activo en el este de Francia durante la primavera y el verano de este año, periodo en el que el virus circuló de forma intensa entre animales, con casos esporádicos detectados en pequeños rumiantes y caballos.

articles.title: NVIDIA veut en finir avec les saccades en jeu : ses nouveaux pilotes changent la donne
articles.summary:
Avec les pilotes GeForce 621.01, NVIDIA active l’Advanced Shader Delivery de Microsoft sur ses cartes RTX. Les shaders arrivent précompilés, ce qui supprime l’attente du premier lancement et les saccades liées à la compilation en pleine partie.
Les nouveaux pilotes NVIDIA préparent les shaders à l’avance : au lieu de compiler sur votre machine, le jeu récupère une version déjà adaptée à votre carte et à votre pilote. D’après NVIDIA, cette attente pouvait atteindre 30 minutes sur les configuration les plus modestes, au premier lancement comme après une mise à jour de pilote.
Des shaders compilés chez Microsoft, téléchargés avec le jeu
Le principe tient en deux étapes. Les studios enregistrent les shaders de leur jeu sous DirectX 12, puis les serveurs de Microsoft les compilent pour des centaines de milliers de combinaisons de cartes et de pilotes. Au téléchargement, l’application Xbox pour PC récupère la version qui correspond à la machine, y compris pour un jeu acheté sur Steam.
Selon NVIDIA, la bibliothèque de shaders de Microsoft couvre déjà presque 100 % des cas. Concrètement, les saccades provoquées par une compilation en cours de partie disparaissent elles aussi. C’est un fléau bien connu des joueurs PC, là où les consoles s’en sortent parce que leur matériel est identique d’une machine à l’autre.

Sé que una reserva estratégica de sirope parece un chiste, pero tiene tanto sentido que lo que explica Goulet es un enorme problema.
Canadá produce más de tres cuartas partes del sirope del mundo y nueve de cada 10 de esos litros salen de Quebec. De hecho, allí, las 8.400 empresas del sector funcionan como un cártel que reparte la producción y vende de forma conjunta. Esa reserva estratégica es el "enlace" del aceite de oliva: el mecanismo de reserva que ayuda a controlar el precio.
Eso es lo que se ha quedado a cero. Y, paradójicamente, ha sido por un éxito.
La OPEP del sirope. El mecanismo es sencillo: lo que no se vende un año, se pasteuriza y se almacena. Lo pagan con una cuota propia los mismos fabricantes. La reserva se creó en el año 2000 porque la cosecha de sirope depende, como todo, de ciertas condiciones climáticas. La posibilidad de que algún año no hubiera suficiente sirope para todos estaba ahí.
Ocurrió, de hecho, en 2008. Y, en 2012, se descubrió un estrambótico robo de unos 10.000 barriles en el almacén de Saint-Louis-de-Blandford. Pero esa es otra historia (que tiene serie y todo).

articles.title: LTO roadmap extends to 365 TB per cartridge as tape storage refuses to die — AI boom spurs relevance of cheap, airgapped storage
articles.summary:
LTO roadmap extends to 365 TB per cartridge as tape storage refuses to die —25-year-old format sees 400x capacity increase without changing form factor
HPE, IBM, and Quantum will keep developing LTO as demand booms.
In a world where SSDs with up to 256TB capacity are about to enter the scene to compete against hard disk drives that store over 40TB, magnetic tape storage may seem archaic. However, the 25-year-old Linear Tape-Open (LTO) format continues to evolve at a rather impressive pace.
The current LTO-10 generation stores up to 40TB of uncompressed data per cartridge, while HPE, IBM, and Quantum — the companies behind the LTO Program — now envision LTO-14 cartridges with up to 365TB of native capacity. But capacity is not the only advantage of LTO. In fact, the consortium has deliberately slowed its capacity roadmap in a bid to prioritize reliability, cost per terabyte, and manageable backup and recovery times over the previous goal of doubling capacity with every generation.
LTO began in 2000 with the LTO-1 format, which stored just 100GB of data natively and transferred it at 20 MB/s. Since then, capacity increased to 200GB with LTO-2, 400GB with LTO-3, 800GB with LTO-4, 1.5TB with LTO-5, 2.5TB with LTO-6, 6TB with LTO-7, 12TB with LTO-8, and 18TB with LTO-9.
The original LTO-10 media introduced in 2025 increased native capacity to 30TB, whereas an extended-length LTO-10 cartridge announced later increased it further to 40TB.

La Commission européenne soupçonne Booking.com de ne pas avoir évalué avec sérieux, ni réduit efficacement, les risques d’annonces frauduleuses et de phishing. Les autorités européennes vérifient aussi que les logements mis en avant contre paiement sont bien présentés comme des publicités.
La Commission européenne a ouvert hier une procédure formelle contre Booking.com au titre du règlement sur les services numériques (DSA). Trois sujets sont passés au crible : les fausses annonces, les arnaques qui exploitent les données de réservation et les annonces« boostées ».
Fausses annonces, messagerie détournée, publicités floues : ce que Bruxelles veut vérifier
Booking.com est classée VLOP (Very Large Online Platform) depuis le 25 avril 2023, un statut réservé aux plateformes de plus de 45 millions d’utilisateurs dans l’UE. Les articles 34 et 35 du DSA lui imposent d’identifier régulièrement les risques que son service peut créer, de les évaluer, puis de les réduire. Il y a tout d'abord les fausses inscriptions (logements inexistants, usurpation d’identité, hébergements non conformes). Selon The Register, la Commission vise notamment des personnes qui se font passer pour le propriétaire d’un bien qu’elles ne possèdent pas.
Le deuxième sujet concerne le phishing. La Commission regarde comment les données de réservation et d’invité sont partagées avec les hébergeurs, comment la messagerie de Booking.com est conçue, et si des garde-fous empêchent leur détournement. Elle soupçonne aussi…

Os desenvolvedores voluntários do PHP escreveram em um comunicado hoje que os problemas têm gravidade 9,2 de uma escala de 10 e afetam servidores que executam PHP 5.4 e versões posteriores.
As falhas permitem que hackers controlem servidores de sites remotamente, sem precisar de senha, e estão relacionadas ao gerenciamento de memória durante o processamento de requisições HTTP. De acordo com os desenvolvedores, “não existem soluções definitivas; a atualização é a única opção segura”.
A Cloudflare, empresa de infraestrutura e segurança web, afirmou que também identificou as falhas, rastreadas como CVE-2026-109618 e CVE-2026-109619 e conhecidas como php2shell. A companhia ativou proteções automáticas em seu firewall de aplicações web (WAF) cerca de nove horas antes da divulgação pública. A medida abrange usuários do plano gratuito que têm o recurso ativado, mas não dispensa a atualização dos servidores.

Account numbers, balances, passwords, one-time passcodes, card details and government identity numbers such as PAN or Aadhaar are not among the categories the filing lists. articles.title: SAP delivers record quarterly revenue as its autonomous enterprise strategy picks up speed - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
SAP delivers record quarterly revenue as its autonomous enterprise strategy picks up speed
Europe’s biggest software company SAP SE delivered record-breaking quarterly revenue after surpassing the €10 billion ($11.2 billion) barrier for the first time earlier today, while delivering a 26% increase in its current cloud backlog and lifting its revenue outlook for the full year. Its stock gained barely over a percentage point in daily trading, but stayed flat after-hours.
The Germany-based firm reported earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of €1.89 per share on total sales of €10.27 billion, outperforming analysts who had expected earnings of just €1.83 per share on revenue of €10.10 billion.
SAP said its third-quarter cloud revenue increased 25% to €6.67 billion, while its non-IFRS operating profit rose to €3.03 billion, up 18% from the same period one year earlier. The company’s cloud backlog rose 26%, to €24.11 billion, ahead of the 24% to 25% growth forecast by analysts. The company also maintained its full-year operating profit outlook at €11.8 billion to €12.2 billion, which it first revealed in July.
SAP’s order book is seen as a bellwether for broader enterprise software spending because its software sits at the heart of many of the world’s largest companies, powering their accounting and payroll systems.

articles.title: Demandan a creadores de Fortnite y Roblox por provocarle “adicción, angustia y depresión” en su adolescencia
articles.summary:
Un joven de 23 años inició una demanda contra Epic Games y Roblox Corporation, a las que acusa de haberle provocado adicción, angustia y depresión durante su adolescencia a través de los videojuegos Fortnite y Roblox.
Dawson Little, residente de San Francisco, Estados Unidos, presentó el caso ante un tribunal de esa ciudad y sostiene que las compañías utilizan sistemas diseñados para generar dependencia en los jugadores más jóvenes.
Un adolescente convertido en demandante

Según su versión, las consecuencias de ese consumo se manifestaron con el paso del tiempo y ahora se traducen en una relación problemática con los videojuegos. En su demanda, atribuye a las plataformas la causa de una “angustia emocional grave, ansiedad, depresión, disminución de las interacciones sociales, falta de interés en otros pasatiempos y síntomas de abstinencia como rabia, ira y arrebatos físicos”, informó Kotaku.
El joven afirma que estos efectos derivaron en una caída drástica de sus calificaciones académicas, lo que terminó en su expulsión del colegio.
Condicionamiento operante como argumento central

articles.title: Airbnb ne veut plus que les voyageurs fassent le ménage : les propriétaires sont furieux
articles.summary:
Airbnb va interdire aux propriétaires d’imposer certaines corvées ménagères à leurs voyageurs, comme défaire les lits ou laver la vaisselle avant leur départ. Une décision qui devrait soulager les vacanciers, mais qui provoque déjà la colère de nombreux hôtes.
Vous avez déjà loué un Airbnb et découvert, la veille de votre départ, une liste de tâches ménagères longue comme le bras ? Entre les draps à retirer, la vaisselle à laver et les poubelles à sortir, certains séjours se terminent parfois par une petite séance de ménage. Le tout alors que des frais de nettoyage figurent déjà sur la facture. Airbnb semble avoir entendu les critiques et vient d’annoncer de nouvelles règles pour encadrer les demandes des propriétaires. Ces derniers, en revanche, ne voient pas forcément cette décision d’un très bon œil.
Airbnb met fin aux listes de corvées interminables

Les propriétaires ne pourront plus exiger des tâches nécessitant un effort ou un temps important, normalement prises en charge par une personne chargée du ménage. Airbnb cite plusieurs exemples : défaire les lits, laver et ranger la vaisselle ou encore transporter les poubelles à l’extérieur de la propriété.

The next game in the series was first announced in November 2020 and teased that December with an official trailer on EA’s Mass Effect YouTube channel. articles.title: U.S. Orders DeepSeek Removed From Federal Civilian Systems, Bans New Purchases
articles.summary:
U.S. federal civilian agencies must remove DeepSeek products from their information technology systems, along with any third-party products or services "developed using DeepSeek implementations," under a Department of Homeland Security order.
They may also no longer buy information technology products or services from the Chinese AI developer or its affiliates
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin issued the order, dated July 24, 2026, under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018, and the department published it in the Federal Register on October 20. The notice does not define "DeepSeek implementations."
The order names Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd., the developer of the R1 and V3 models, and covers its affiliates as defined in federal acquisition rules. The company's privacy policy says it collects, processes and stores users' personal data in the People's Republic of China.
Under the 2018 law, the Federal Acquisition Security Council recommends exclusion and removal orders, and three officials may issue them: the Secretary of Homeland Security for civilian agencies, the Secretary of Defense for the Defense Department and national security systems, and the Director of National Intelligence for the intelligence community.
The DeepSeek order therefore covers only what civilian agencies buy and run. It does not restrict companies or the public.

Os clientes da Claro podem até procurar, mas não vão encontrar celulares da Oppo nas lojas da operadora. Eu tive acesso ao comunicado assinado pela Diretoria de Estratégia de Produtos Eletrônicos da Claro. O material confidencial indica uma série de medidas contra os produtos da Oppo, como a retirada dos aparelhos que ficam habitualmente nas chamadas mesas de degustação. Eles devem ser mantidos no estoque, longe do público. Os funcionários da Claro também foram orientados a retirar os materiais oficiais de comunicação da Oppo.

articles.title: Cómo borrar el historial de Google en distintos dispositivos y para qué sirve hacerlo
articles.summary:
El historial de Google reúne en un solo registro las búsquedas, los sitios visitados, las ubicaciones, los videos reproducidos y la actividad de las apps vinculadas a una cuenta. Borrarlo es posible desde dos frentes: la cuenta de Google, que sincroniza los datos entre todos los dispositivos, y el navegador instalado en cada equipo, que guarda su propia copia local de la navegación.
Eliminar esa información no es solo una cuestión de orden. Permite resguardar la privacidad frente a terceros que comparten un mismo dispositivo, reduce la publicidad dirigida basada en búsquedas recientes y ayuda a liberar memoria local al limpiar la caché y las cookies acumuladas.
Para qué sirve eliminar el historial de búsquedas
Borrar el historial cumple varias funciones a la vez. La primera es la privacidad: evita que familiares o compañeros de trabajo con acceso físico a un dispositivo puedan ver qué se buscó o qué páginas se visitaron.
También incide en los algoritmos de recomendación. Plataformas como YouTube, Google News o el feed de Discover construyen sus sugerencias a partir del consumo previo, de modo que limpiar el historial permite reiniciar esas recomendaciones desde cero.
Existe además un efecto sobre la publicidad. Al eliminar el rastro de búsquedas recientes, se reduce la cantidad de anuncios asociados a productos o servicios investigados poco tiempo atrás.
Por último, cumple una función de seguridad y rendimiento: disminuye los datos personales almacenados en la nube ante un ev…

articles.title: Meta hit with $25 billion fine for deceiving users on privacy - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Meta hit with $25 billion fine for deceiving users on privacy
Meta Platforms Inc. was ordered to pay $25 billion in penalties today after a jury found the company had misled its users on how it protects and uses their data.
In what is one of the largest fines ever leveled against a tech giant, a jury in a Santa Fe, New Mexico, found the company guilty deceiving its users. The case, going back 10 years, is related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal when Meta was Facebook Inc.
Following a two-week trial last month, the jury ruled against Meta, concluding that the company had committed 43 million violations of the state’s unfair practices act. With each violation carrying a penalty of up to $5,000, the state was originally awarded $219.5 billion, but Judge Francis Mathew reduced the fine to $25 billion.
“The extraordinary number of willful violations found by the jury, the duration and repetition of the conduct, the breadth of subjects on which violations occurred, the involvement of senior Facebook leadership, the size of New Mexico audiences reached, and the clear intentional and systematic nature of Facebook’s repeated misstatements established in the trial record support the highest level of penalty allowed by the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act — $5,000 per violation found by the jury,” Judge Mathew wrote in the filing.
Meta is paying a heavy price for allegations that its platforms harm the public. In August, it agreed to a $17.1 billion settlement with dozens of U.S. stat…

Attackers took control of more than 300 Tor exit relays in early October and used them to redirect SSH connections to servers that stole login passwords, a researcher found.
Exit relays are the last hop in a Tor circuit, where traffic leaves the network for its destination. Only a password login to an SSH server made through Tor between October 1 and 5, after accepting the interception server's host key, could have been captured.
The Tor Project began flagging relays on October 4, and by October 5, none remained in the consensus, the list of relays that Tor clients use. At the peak on October 4, the relays carrying the attacker's exit policy made up 7.46% of Tor's exit capacity, measured by consensus weight, according to an analysis of public Tor directory data posted to the tor-relays mailing list.
The researcher, who publishes as kaba, scanned all of Tor's roughly 3,000 exits on October 2 and found 333 redirecting SSH to the same 12 interception servers. The directory-data analysis counts 377 relays run by 59 operators that switched to the attacker's exit policy between October 1 and 4, which it calls "a policy match, not proof of compromise."
How the Hijacked Exits Intercepted SSH
An exit relay only carries traffic to the ports its exit policy allows. The attackers rewrote that policy in the relays' torrc configuration files to allow port 22 (the SSH port), enabling SSH on 342 relays that had blocked it. Another 24 relays that had not been exits at all became exits.

Additionally, with the code signing certificates, an application you download can be shown as completely legitimate from, say, Microsoft or Google.

Intel's Core Ultra 9 4995HX looks set to be the fastest Nova Lake chip for laptops. Leaker Jaykihn on X has confirmed that the 4995HX uses an 8+16+4+2 layout, meaning 8 P-cores, 16 E-cores, 4 LPE cores, and 2 Xe3 GPU cores. The same post lists the Core Ultra 9 4970H as 4+8+4+12, so 16 CPU cores and a 12-core Xe3P iGPU. That is the same core count as Panther Lake's flagship Core Ultra X9 388H, so any gains here should come from the new Coyote Cove P-cores, Arctic Wolf E-cores, and Xe3P graphics rather than extra cores. The tiny iGPU on the 4995HX is less of a concern, since HX chips almost always end up paired with a discrete GPU anyway. Jaykihn also put the final 8+16 HX compute tile, built on TSMC N2P, at 14.8 x 6.6 mm, or roughly 98 mm², shortly after die shots of both chips surfaced. articles.title: The Harness Is the Hard Part of Agentic Pentesting
articles.summary:
An AppSec team can point an AI agent running on a general-purpose model at its own web apps with little setup. Sure, the model writes the attacks. But everything that makes those attacks safe to run against production and worth acting on afterward lives in the harness around the model. The harness is where the engineering in AI pentesting sits. The Hugging Face intrusion OpenAI disclosed in July showed what happens when that harness gives way, even inside an OpenAI evaluation built to contain the agents.
Why Each Control Takes Rigorous Engineering
Let’s take a closer look at the attack different stages and the role AI agents can take there
Scope
A pentesting agent makes thousands of decisions about where to send its next request, and the model judges each one against a rule written in plain language. A web app’s real boundary often extends past one domain through redirects and calls to outside services. Enforcing scope means code that inspects every request before it leaves, and OWASP’s 2026 guidance routes privileged actions through a deterministic policy engine that checks them at execution time, outside the model.
Credentials
Finding exposed credentials is part of what a pentest does, so the agent regularly comes across working keys outside its assignment. Which of those it may use, for what, and when a person gets involved are policy decisions that the code around the model applies on every attempt.

articles.title: What does it actually mean to treat data as an asset?

What does it actually mean to treat data as an asset?
Turning data into a defined, governed and commercially usable asset
We understand what it means to own a house, a car, a share in a company, a patent or a trademark. In each case, there is an established legal framework that defines the asset, establishes who holds it and enables it to be sold, transferred, financed or protected.
Data is more complicated. A business may have spent decades building a valuable body of data that it protects and depends upon, yet establishing precisely what constitutes that asset, and what rights are attached to it, is far less straightforward.
That uncertainty has commercial consequences. It can make data harder to value, license or share with confidence, leaving transactions heavily dependent on contracts and trust between the parties rather than an independently verifiable understanding of what the data is and how it may be used.
Aga Strandskov, Head of Data Strategy, Digital Isle of Man
This is a challenge we have been exploring in the Isle of Man through the development of the Data Asset Foundations framework, which establishes the statutory basis for defined, governed data to be recognized as an asset.
With the framework now moving into implementation, a much broader question remains relevant for businesses: if we are serious about treating data as an asset, what does that actually require?
What makes data an asset?

Facial recognition technology must be scrutinized across all applications
Facial recognition technology (FRT) is fast becoming part of everyday life in the UK.

CEO of Face-Int UK and Europe.

articles.title: Generative AI Is Erasing Behavioral Tells, Weakening Behavior-Only Detection, Proofpoint Reports
articles.summary:
Generative AI has changed what a malicious email looks like. Messages that once gave themselves away through clumsy wording, generic pretexts, and reused templates now arrive fluent, personalized, and unique to each recipient, and the behavioral signals email filters have relied on for years are fading as a result.
Proofpoint shared several examples of the shift at its Protect 2026 conference. In one, a single threat actor contacted more than 30 real estate agents at the same company, each from a different account, about a different property, and in different words, before closing every thread with the same request: join a video meeting.
Federal data points the same way. The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center counted more than 22,000 complaints involving AI in 2025, with nearly $900 million in associated losses, and logged 24,768 business email compromise (BEC) complaints with about $3.05 billion in reported losses, according to its 2025 Internet Crime Report.
What AI Changed
Email filters were built for attackers who had to cut corners. Researching a target, writing convincingly in a second language, impersonating a supplier, and producing enough variants to defeat signatures all took time, so attackers reused templates and infrastructure, and that reuse left patterns. Behavioral detection learned to spot them: new infrastructure, awkward language, odd timing, and requests that did not fit the conversation.

articles.title: China-Aligned Bronze Sandcastle Abuses Sandboxie DLL Sideloading to Deploy Backdoors
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a previously undocumented China-aligned threat cluster known as Bronze Sandcastle that has been observed targeting organizations in Asia and Africa since mid-2025.
"The most distinctive technical marker for Bronze Sandcastle is its consistent use of Sandboxie DLL sideloading," Sophos security researcher Gabor Szappanos said in a post published Tuesday.
Between August 2025 and August 2026, attacks mounted by the threat actor have resulted in victims in the Philippines, Taiwan, Afghanistan, Namibia, and likely South Korea. Evidence indicates that Bronze Sandcastle is most active in the UTC+8 time zone.
DLL sideloading is a popular adversarial technique that exploits the way Windows loads DLL files, allowing an attacker to trick a legitimate program into loading a malicious DLL.
When an application is launched, it needs to load various DLLs in order to function correctly. If the application does not provide the full path to a required DLL, the operating system looks for it in a predetermined sequence of directories.
An attacker can take advantage of this behavior by planting a malicious DLL with the same name as a legitimate one in a location that Windows searches before the folder that contains the actual DLL. Thus, when the legitimate application starts, it proceeds to load and run the malicious DLL, giving the attacker a way in to the system.

articles.title: Google Chrome Adds ClickFix Warnings to Stop Users From Running Malicious Commands
articles.summary:
Google on Tuesday said it's rolling out improved safeguards in its Chrome browser to secure users against ClickFix attacks when Enhanced Protection is enabled.
ClickFix is a popular social engineering technique in which bad actors trick users into copying and pasting malicious code directly into their computer's operating system, thereby bypassing conventional security controls.
As part of these attacks, unsuspecting users who land on legitimate-but-compromised sites or click on malicious ads are redirected to phishing landing pages that display fake Cloudflare or Google reCAPTCHA verification or other non-existent errors and instruct users to copy and paste a command on the Windows Run dialog (or the Mac Terminal app) to address it.
The moment a user presses the Enter key after pasting the command, it triggers a multi-stage infection chain that leads to the deployment of malware, such as information stealers or remote access trojans. In an attempt to blend in with regular activity and evade detection, the commands often make use of living-off-the-land (LotL) tools like PowerShell or cmd.exe to download next-stage payloads.
A key reason why ClickFix remains an effective initial access method is that it flips the script on traditional phishing. Instead of exploiting sophisticated vulnerabilities or getting a user to click on suspicious links, it tricks them into opening the front door themselves under the pretext of troubleshooting a commonplace issue.

PHP has released emergency updates that fix two critical flaws in the language itself, letting an attacker without an account run code on a web server. The fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and the PHP team says only updating fully protects a server.
The flaws, together called PHP2Shell, sit in the PHP runtime, not in any application, so a site is exposed even when its own code is secure. The risk is highest on servers using Apache's mod_php, where a working exploit triggers the attack before any application code runs.
Both flaws are rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale and carry the identifiers CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. PHP published them around the scheduled release time of 14:00 UTC on October 21, a day after details leaked ahead of a planned October 22 disclosure.
Researchers at Wiz, Calif, and OpenAI found and reported the flaws, which affect nearly every PHP version back to PHP 5.4.
Who Is Affected
Every PHP installation that serves web requests is at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed, according to the PHP security advisory.
Because the flaws are in the engine rather than in any site's code, even a simple "Hello World" page on a vulnerable PHP version can be attacked.
The advisory singles out mod_php as the highest risk, with a demonstrated exploit in which a single unauthenticated request triggers the attack before any application code runs. PHP-FPM behaves differently, because it shuts the worker down w…

AMD Readies Official Ryzen Overclocking Driver for Linux
AMD is reportedly working on official Ryzen overclocking controls for Linux. Per Phoronix, AMD engineer Shyam Sundar S K has posted a three-patch series for a new driver called AOD, short for AMD Overclocking Driver, to the platform-driver-x86 mailing list. It is a WMI driver that talks to the same firmware interface Ryzen Master uses on Windows, with all of its controls exposed through sysfs. For now, that covers PPT, TDC, and EDC limits along with their supported ranges, a platform-level SMT toggle, and a read-only memory clock readout. Notably, Ryzen Master itself isn't coming to Linux with this. AMD seems to be following the same approach it took with its amdgpu graphics driver, handling the kernel side and leaving the GUI to third-party tools such as CoreCtrl and to desktop environments.
There are a few catches, however. Power limit changes are stored in firmware and only kick in after a reboot. AMD's existing HSMP interface works the other way around, applying limits instantly but losing them on restart. The PPT, TDC, and EDC attributes are also write-only, since the firmware doesn't report the currently active values. The SMT switch, meanwhile, behaves more like a BIOS option than the kernel's nosmt boot parameter. Apparently, the firmware supports many more commands than the initial patches wire up, so more controls could arrive later. The patches are still under review, and there is…

Les passkeys, ou clés d’accès, évitent qu’un site stocke un secret partagé, comme un mot de passe, afin qu’ils ne tombent pas entre les mains de pirates lors d’une fuite de données. La cryptographie qui les protège pourrait toutefois être cassée un jour par un ordinateur quantique.

Nous rapportions en mai 2023 que 1Password allait permettre de sauvegarder, gérer et synchroniser les passkeys entre plusieurs écosystèmes. Trois ans plus tard, l'éditeur s'intéresse à leur durée de vie. Un passkey reste souvent utilisé pendant des années, et l'entreprise préfère donc proposer tôt une version résistante au quantique. Celui-ci repose sur ML-DSA, un algorithme de signature numérique standardisé par le NIST en 2024. C’est cette signature qui permet à votre appareil de prouver son identité au site.
Mais les choses vont plus vite que prévu. Et depuis 2023, l’estimation de la puissance nécessaire pour casser ces signatures a changé.
